instruments.name: GRI 405: Diversity and Equal Opportunity 2016 (Disclosures 405-1 and 405-2)
instruments.status: In force. Will be replaced by GRI 109: Diversity and Inclusion 2027 (which takes over 405-1) and GRI 105: Remuneration and Working Time 2027 (which takes over 405-2) once their effective date is set.
instruments.effective: Issued by the GSSB in 2016. Effective for reports published on or after 1 July 2018. Still usable on 12 Oct 2026 because no effective date has been set for the 2027 labor standards.
instruments.coverage: Any organisation reporting 'in accordance with' or 'with reference to' GRI. No size threshold. The disclosures apply when diversity and equal opportunity is a material topic under GRI 3, and an omission is allowed if a reason is given. The reporting entity is the boundary defined in GRI 2-2, normally the consolidated group.

measures.name: 405-1-a Gender of governance body members
measures.definition: Percentage of individuals within the organization's governance bodies in each diversity category: gender; age group (under 30, 30-50, over 50); other indicators such as minority or vulnerable groups. This is a GRI requirement when the topic is material.
measures.population: Members of the governance bodies the organisation identifies (board and its committees)
measures.period: Reporting period; no snapshot date is fixed
mapsTo: Official: the GRI-ESRS Interoperability Index maps 405-1 to ESRS 2 GOV-1 board gender diversity (row not re-verified). ESRS states a female-to-male ratio, not a percentage
Official: WEF SCM core metric 'Governance body composition' cites GRI 102-22 and 405-1a

By definition: GRI 2-9-c-v; EU Women on Boards Directive 2022/2381; India BRSR participation of women in BoD/KMP; Japan securities-report female director ratio; Equileap criterion 1; Bloomberg GEI board share

measures.name: 405-1-b Gender of employees in each employee category
measures.definition: Percentage of employees per employee category in each diversity category, including gender. The organisation defines its own employee categories (for example senior management, middle management, technical, administrative).
measures.basis: Headcount or FTE, whichever method the organisation states under GRI 2-7
measures.population: Employees only (non-employee workers excluded), by employee category
measures.period: Reporting period; end-of-period or average, as stated under GRI 2-7-c
mapsTo: Official: WEF SCM core metric 'Diversity and inclusion' cites GRI 405-1b
Official: the GRI-ESRS Index maps 405-1 to ESRS S1 diversity metrics (row not re-verified). Now ESRS (2026) S1-5 para 20(a) headcount by gender and S1-8 para 27 top-management gender split
By definition: SASB TC-SI-330a.3, FN-AC-330a.1, FN-IB-330a.1, SV-PS-330a.1; SDG 5.5.2 (management categories only); Equileap criteria 2-4; WEPs Essential Indicators; ISO 30414 workforce diversity

measures.name: 405-2-a Ratio of basic salary of women to men
measures.definition: Ratio of the basic salary of women to men for each employee category, by significant locations of operation. Under 405-2-b the organisation must also state its definition of 'significant locations of operation'. The GRI glossary defines basic salary as the fixed, minimum amount paid to an employee for their duties, excluding overtime and bonuses.
measures.unit: Ratio, women to men (e.g. 0.92:1), one per category per location
measures.basis: Base pay only. The standard does not fix the time unit (annual or hourly) or whether the average is a mean or a median; in practice it is usually average annual base salary
measures.population: Employees in each employee category at each significant location. No company-wide figure is required
mapsTo: Official: the GRI-ESRS Index maps 405-2 to ESRS S1-16 paras 97-98 (2023 ESRS). This is a topic mapping, not numeric equivalence. Now ESRS (2026) S1-15 para 41(a)
Official: WEF SCM core metric 'Pay equality' is adapted from GRI 405-2
By definition: EU Pay Transparency Directive 2023/970 Art 9(1)(g) (gap by category of workers, basic pay); Japan Women's Advancement Act wage-gap disclosure (also a women-to-men ratio)
Successor: GRI 105 basic gender pay gap (2027)

measures.name: 405-2-a Ratio of remuneration of women to men
measures.definition: Ratio of the remuneration of women to men for each employee category, by significant locations of operation. The GRI glossary defines remuneration as basic salary plus additional amounts paid to a worker: service-based pay, cash and equity bonuses, benefit payments, overtime, time owed and allowances.
measures.unit: Ratio, women to men, per category per location
measures.basis: Total pay. Time unit and mean or median are not fixed
measures.population: Employees in each employee category at each significant location
mapsTo: Official: the GRI-ESRS Index maps 405-2 to ESRS S1-16 (2023). Closest numeric analogue is ESRS (2026) S1-15 para 41(a), which uses total gross hourly pay and the mean

By definition: Australia WGEA total-remuneration gap; UK GPG Regulations 2017 mean/median hourly pay gap (ordinary pay); India BRSR P5 EI-3 median remuneration by gender; Japan wage-gap disclosure (total wages)

instruments.publicAccess: The standard is free to download from GRI after a registration form. Data are published in companies' public sustainability reports with a GRI content index; there is no central register.

instruments.name: GRI 401: Employment 2016 (Disclosures 401-1 and 401-3)
instruments.status: In force. 401-1 is being replaced by GRI 104: Employment 2027 (approved by the GSSB on 16 July 2026). 401-3 is being replaced by GRI 107: Working Parents and Caregivers 2027 (final draft June 2026, no re-exposure).
instruments.effective: Effective for reports published on or after 1 July 2018
instruments.coverage: GRI reporters for whom employment is a material topic. No size threshold. Boundary set under GRI 2-2.

measures.name: 401-1 New hires and employee turnover by gender
measures.definition: Total number and rate of new employee hires during the reporting period, by age group, gender and region (401-1-a). Total number and rate of employee turnover, by age group, gender and region (401-1-b). Rates use total employees at the end of the reporting period.
measures.period: Reporting period; the rate denominator is headcount at period end
mapsTo: Official: WEF SCM core metric 'Employment and wealth generation' (hires and turnover by age group and gender) is sourced from GRI 401-1
Official: the GRI-ESRS Index maps 401-1 to ESRS S1 turnover (row not re-verified). ESRS turnover has no gender split
By definition: WEPs Essential Indicator on new hires; Bloomberg GEI hiring and attrition fields

measures.name: 401-3 Parental leave by gender
measures.definition: Five items, each by gender: (a) employees entitled to parental leave; (b) employees who took it; (c) employees who returned to work in the period after leave ended; (d) employees still employed 12 months after returning; (e) return-to-work and retention rates. Return-to-work rate = returned / due to return x 100. Retention rate = retained 12 months after return / returned in prior period(s) x 100.
measures.population: Employees entitled to or taking parental leave as defined by the organisation and national law
measures.period: Reporting period; retention looks back 12 months
mapsTo: Official: the GRI-ESRS Index maps 401-3 to ESRS S1-15 (2023) family-related leave (row not re-verified). ESRS (2026) S1-14 para 39 keeps only the % of employees entitled, with no gender split, so the mapping narrows

By definition: Japan male childcare-leave uptake rate (securities report and Child Care and Family Care Leave Act); Bloomberg GEI parental-leave retention question; Equileap criterion 8 (policy, not a rate)
Successor: GRI 107 (2027)

instruments.publicAccess: Free standard; data appear in public company reports
interop: GRI-ESRS-INDEX

instruments.name: GRI 404: Training and Education 2016 (Disclosures 404-1 and 404-3)
instruments.status: In force. Under revision in the GRI Labor project (Training and Education exposure draft, Feb-Apr 2025).
instruments.effective: Effective for reports published on or after 1 July 2018
instruments.coverage: GRI reporters for whom training is a material topic

measures.name: 404-1 Average training hours by gender
measures.definition: Average hours of training the organization's employees have undertaken during the reporting period, by gender and by employee category. Calculated as total training hours for women (or men) divided by the number of women (or men) employees.
measures.population: Employees, by gender and employee category
mapsTo: Official: WEF SCM core metric 'Training provided' is sourced from GRI 404-1

Official: the GRI-ESRS Index maps 404-1 to ESRS S1-13 (2023) training hours by gender (row not re-verified). ESRS (2026) S1-12 para 35 asks only for the average training hours per employee, with no gender split
By definition: India BRSR Principle 3 training indicator (share of employees trained, by gender, not hours)

measures.name: 404-3 Performance and career development reviews by gender
measures.definition: Percentage of total employees, by gender and by employee category, who received a regular performance and career development review during the reporting period.
measures.population: Employees, by gender and employee category
mapsTo: Official: the GRI-ESRS Index maps 404-3 to ESRS S1-13 (2023) reviews by gender (row not re-verified). ESRS (2026) S1-12 has no gender split
By definition: India BRSR Principle 3 performance and career development review indicator (by gender)

instruments.publicAccess: Free standard; data appear in public company reports

instruments.name: GRI 406: Non-discrimination 2016 (Disclosure 406-1)
instruments.status: In force. Will be replaced by GRI 110: Non-discrimination and Equal Opportunity 2027 (exposure draft comment closed 15 Sept 2025; GSSB approval expected Q4 2026 to 2027).
instruments.effective: Effective for reports published on or after 1 July 2018
instruments.coverage: GRI reporters for whom non-discrimination is material

measures.name: 406-1 Incidents of discrimination
measures.definition: Total number of incidents of discrimination during the reporting period, plus the status of the incidents and actions taken. The grounds include sex as well as the other ILO grounds (race, colour, religion, political opinion, national extraction, social origin). The count is not split by gender.
measures.basis: Count of incidents raised through legal actions, complaints or the organisation's own identification
measures.population: Employees and other individuals affected by the organisation's operations
mapsTo: Official: the GRI-ESRS Index maps 406-1 to ESRS S1-17 (2023) incidents of discrimination including harassment (row not re-verified)
By definition: WEF SCM expanded metric 'Discrimination and harassment incidents'
Successor: GRI 110 (2027)

instruments.publicAccess: Free standard; data appear in public company reports
interop: GRI-ESRS-INDEX
WEF-SCM
GRI-LABOR-2027
instruments.quote: Total number of incidents of discrimination during the reporting period.

instruments.name: GRI 2: General Disclosures 2021 (2-7 Employees; 2-9 Governance structure and composition)
instruments.status: In force. Every GRI report must include it, whatever its material topics.
instruments.effective: Effective 1 January 2023
instruments.coverage: All GRI reporters. 2-7 and 2-9 are required for 'in accordance' reporting. The reporting entity is defined in 2-2.

measures.name: 2-7 Employees by gender and contract type
measures.definition: Total number of employees, broken down by gender and by region. Also the numbers of permanent, temporary, non-guaranteed-hours, full-time and part-time employees, each by gender and region. Under 2-7-c the organisation must state whether the figures are headcount, FTE or another method, and whether they are at period end, a period average or another method.
measures.population: Employees, split permanent / temporary / non-guaranteed hours / full-time / part-time
measures.period: End of reporting period, period average or another stated method
mapsTo: Official: the GRI-ESRS Index maps 2-7 to ESRS S1-6 (2023) (row not re-verified). Now ESRS (2026) S1-5 para 20(a) headcount by gender and 20(c) permanent/temporary by gender
By definition: India BRSR Section A employees and workers by gender (permanent / other than permanent); Australia WGEA workforce profile

measures.name: 2-9-c-v Gender composition of the highest governance body
measures.definition: Describe the composition of the highest governance body and its committees by, among other things, gender and under-represented social groups.
measures.population: Highest governance body and its committees
mapsTo: Official: WEF SCM 'Governance body composition' (cites GRI 102-22, the predecessor of 2-9)
By definition: GRI 405-1-a; ESRS 2 GOV-1 board gender diversity ratio

instruments.publicAccess: Free standard; data appear in public company reports
interop: GRI-ESRS-INDEX
WEF-SCM
instruments.quote: total number of employees, and a breakdown of this total by gender and by region

instruments.name: GRI 202: Market Presence 2016 (Disclosure 202-1)
instruments.status: In force. Being folded into GRI 105: Remuneration and Working Time 2027.
instruments.effective: Effective for reports published on or after 1 July 2018
instruments.coverage: GRI reporters where a significant share of employees are paid wages subject to minimum-wage rules

measures.name: 202-1-a Entry-level wage by gender relative to the local minimum wage
measures.definition: When a significant proportion of employees are paid wages subject to minimum-wage rules, report the ratio of the entry-level wage, by gender, at significant locations of operation to the minimum wage.
measures.unit: Ratio (entry-level wage / local minimum wage), separately for women and men
measures.basis: Standard entry-level wage rate in the local pay unit
measures.population: Employees at significant locations of operation
mapsTo: Official: WEF SCM core metric 'Wage level' part 1 is sourced from GRI 202-1
By definition: ESRS S1 adequate-wage disclosure (no gender split)
Successor: GRI 105 (2027)

instruments.publicAccess: Free standard; data appear in public company reports

instruments.name: GRI Topic Standards for Labor 2027: GRI 104 Employment, 105 Remuneration and Working Time, 106 Significant Changes for Workers, 107 Working Parents and Caregivers, 109 Diversity and Inclusion, 110 Non-discrimination and Equal Opportunity
instruments.status: Passed in part, not yet in force. The GSSB approved the labor standards (final drafts of GRI 104 and 105) at its 16 July 2026 meeting. GRI 107 was a final draft on 1 June 2026, with no re-exposure needed. GRI 109 and 110 exposure drafts closed on 15 Sept 2025, with GSSB approval expected Q4 2026 to 2027. No formal launch found by 12 Oct 2026; GRI's schedule put final due-process (DPOC) approval in October 2026.
instruments.effective: Not yet set. The drafts read 'EFFECTIVE DATE: [DAY MONTH YEAR]', and the effective date for the whole labor set was put to the 16 July 2026 meeting (outcome not found). Until then GRI 202, 401, 404, 405 and 406 (2016) apply.
instruments.coverage: Same as GRI. The new standards extend scope to workers who are not employees but whose work the organisation controls.

measures.name: GRI 105 basic gender pay gap (exposure-draft wording, disclosure REWO-5)
measures.definition: By significant locations of operation, the percentage difference in average gross basic hourly pay of men and women for each employee category. Mean or median may be used, with gap = (men's - women's) / men's. The organisation states which average it used, headcount or FTE, how part-time hours were treated and whether the gap was adjusted. The final text approved in July 2026 was not verified.
measures.basis: Hourly, gross basic pay, mean or median (stated)
measures.population: Employees, by employee category and significant location
mapsTo: Predecessor: GRI 405-2-a basic-salary ratio. A ratio r becomes a gap 1 - r only on an identical basis
By definition: ESRS (2026) S1-15 para 41(a), also hourly but total pay, mean, company-wide
By definition: EU Pay Transparency Directive 2023/970 Art 9(1)(a), (c) and (g); UK GPG Regulations 2017 mean/median hourly gap (ordinary pay, not basic only); SDG 8.5.1 gap (hours-weighted mean)

measures.name: GRI 109 diversity of governance bodies and employees (exposure draft)
measures.definition: Number and percentage of individuals in governance bodies, and of employees, in each diversity category, including gender and under-represented social groups. Wording as it appears in GRI sector-standard drafts; final text pending.
mapsTo: Predecessor: GRI 405-1
By definition: ESRS 2 GOV-1; ESRS (2026) S1-8 para 27

measures.name: GRI 107 family-related leave (final draft)
measures.definition: Successor to 401-3, covering family-related leave, flexible working and caregiver support. Revised requirement 107-1-a asks for the number of days or weeks of leave beyond the legal minimum. Not verified whether the return and retention rates by gender survive.
measures.population: Employees (scope for other workers not verified)
mapsTo: Predecessor: GRI 401-3
By definition: ESRS (2026) S1-14 para 39

instruments.publicAccess: Exposure drafts, final drafts and GSSB papers are public on globalreporting.org; the final standards will be free

instruments.status: Published and voluntary. No revised metric set found after 2020; WEF reported more than 150 companies using it by Jan 2024.

areas.notes:
Scope. This is the global and voluntary layer. Every measure is marked mandatory=false because none of these instruments legally binds a listed company on its own. Within the frameworks: GRI disclosures are 'requirements' for material topics (an omission is allowed with a reason); WEF core metrics are recommended; SASB metrics must be considered (not applied) where IFRS S1 is adopted.

Official interoperability and equivalence documents:
- GRI-ESRS Interoperability Index (EFRAG and GRI, final 22 Nov 2024, draft Nov 2023), plus a GRI-ESRS data-point mapping. It says ESRS reporters can be considered as reporting 'with reference to' GRI.
- ESRS-ISSB Standards Interoperability Guidance (2 May 2024). It covers climate and general concepts only.
- GRI and IFRS Foundation MoU (March 2022) and collaboration statement (24 May 2024). The only joint output so far is a biodiversity pilot.
- GRI-SASB practical guide (April 2021). It is qualitative.
- WEF Stakeholder Capitalism Metrics (2020). Each metric cites its GRI source.
- WEPs Transparency and Accountability Framework (2021). It lists GRI, the WEPs Tool, EDGE and Bloomberg GEI as its sources.
- IFRS 'Using SASB Standards for IFRS S1'.
- No official mapping links SDG 5.5.2 or 8.5.1, ILO, OECD, ISO 30414, Equileap or Bloomberg GEI to the company regimes. The links given for those are by definition only.

Genuinely interoperable:
1. GRI 405-2 (and 2-21) maps to ESRS S1-16 paras 97-98 in the 2023 ESRS. This row was verified in the index; the other GRI workforce rows (2-7, 401-1, 401-3, 404-1, 404-3, 405-1, 406-1 to ESRS S1-6, S1-9, S1-13, S1-15, S1-17 and GOV-1) were not re-verified. The index maps topics and datapoints; it does not make the numbers equivalent.
2. The index predates the revised ESRS (2026), adopted 3 July 2026 as C(2026) 5010 and applicable to financial years from 1 Jan 2027. In the revised set:
   - The gap is now S1-15 para 41(a): average pay, gross hourly, basic plus other remuneration, as a % of men's.
   - Training (S1-12 para 35) and family-leave entitlement (S1-14 para 39) lose their gender splits.
   - Top-management gender (S1-8 para 27) and headcount by gender (S1-5 para 20) remain.
   - As a result, GRI 404-1, 404-3 and 401-3 gender data no longer have an ESRS counterpart. No updated index was found.
3. WEF core metrics are near-copies of GRI 405-1b, 405-2 (extended to ethnicity), 202-1, 404-1, 401-1 and 102-22/2-9, so they are interchangeable with GRI on the same basis.
4. There is no ISSB-ESRS or GRI-ISSB mapping for workforce or gender. IFRS S1 has no gender metric. SASB has diversity metrics only in some industries (e.g. TC-SI-330a.3, FN-AC-330a.1, FN-IB-330a.1, SV-PS-330a.1). The ISSB workforce project is research only, renamed 'Workforce-related Disclosures' on 24 Sept 2026.

Only looks alike:
- Ratio vs gap. GRI 405-2 is a women-to-men ratio by employee category and location, with basic and total pay separate and no fixed time unit or average. ESRS, EU PTD, UK and GRI 105 report a gap, (M - W) / M. A ratio r converts to a gap 1 - r only on identical populations and pay definitions. A company-wide gap cannot be built from category ratios without headcounts and pay totals.
- Gap definitions by regime:

| Regime | Pay measured | Average | Other features |
|---|---|---|---|
| GRI 105 (2027, draft) | Basic hourly pay | Mean or median (stated) | By category and location |
| ESRS (2026) | Total gross hourly pay | Mean | Company-wide |
| EU PTD | Gross annual and hourly pay | Mean and median | Separate variable-pay gaps, quartiles, gaps by category of equal work |
| UK | Hourly ordinary pay, full-pay relevant employees, snapshot date | Mean and median | Separate 12-month bonus gap |
| Japan | Average annual wage | Mean | Women as % of men (a ratio), split all / regular / non-regular |
| Australia WGEA | Total remuneration, annualised FTE | Median (and mean) | |
| India BRSR | Annual remuneration per group (board, KMP, employees, workers) | Median | Plus female share of gross wages |
| OECD | Earnings of full-time employees | Median | Not hourly |
| SDG 8.5.1 | Hourly earnings, economy-wide | Hours-weighted mean | National statistic |

- 'Management' means different things:
  - ESRS top management: two levels below the board.
  - SDG 5.5.2: ISCO-08 groups 11-13 (senior and middle) or major group 1 (including junior).
  - SASB: executive and non-executive management.
  - GRI: categories the company defines.
  - Others: Japan's national manager definitions, Equileap's 'senior management', ISO's 'leadership team'.
- Boards: GRI 405-1a reports a % of each governance body; ESRS GOV-1 reports an average female-to-male ratio.
- SDG, ILO and OECD figures are national statistics. Use them as country benchmarks for company figures, never as company data.
- Equileap and Bloomberg reuse whatever gap a company publishes, so their pay fields mix bases.

Traps:
1. Hourly vs annual. Hourly: UK, ESRS, GRI 105, SDG 8.5.1. Annual: Japan, BRSR, WGEA (annualised FTE). Both: EU PTD. Unspecified: GRI 405-2. Weekly or monthly: OECD. Part-time-heavy workforces swing the annual figures.
2. Mean vs median. ESRS and SDG use the mean. BRSR and OECD use the median. WGEA's headline is the median. UK and EU PTD use both. GRI 105 allows either but the choice must be disclosed. WEF expanded uses the mean.
3. Base vs total. GRI 105 uses basic pay. GRI 405-2 has both. ESRS, WGEA and Japan use total. UK uses ordinary pay plus a separate bonus gap. EU PTD splits basic from variable. Equity, overtime and in-kind treatment differ.
4. Permanent vs all staff.
   - Population: UK uses full-pay relevant employees. ESRS uses all employees by headcount. Japan splits regular and non-regular. BRSR splits employees from workers and board/KMP. GRI 2-7 and 401 cover employees only, while GRI 2027 adds non-employee workers. SDG covers all employees economy-wide. OECD covers full-time workers only.
   - Headcount vs FTE: GRI 2-7 and GRI 105 require the choice to be stated.
5. Snapshot date.
   - Fixed snapshots: UK 5 April (31 March public sector), with bonuses over the 12 months before. WGEA uses a payroll snapshot.
   - Period-based: ESRS headcount at year end or a period average. GRI 2-7 states its method. GRI 401-1 rates use period-end headcount. Japan uses the fiscal year. BRSR uses the fiscal year.
   - Benchmarks use the latest public data.
6. Reporting entity vs listed group. UK, Japan (law) and WGEA report per legal employer, with thresholds applied per entity; a listed group can publish several UK entity gaps and no group gap. ESRS, IFRS S1 and SASB report on the consolidated group. GRI uses the boundary set in GRI 2-2. BRSR reports for the listed entity, standalone or consolidated as stated.
7. Sign and form. A positive gap means men earn more; a ratio below 1 means women earn less. Japan expresses women's pay as a % of men's. Bloomberg uses adjusted ratios such as 0.99.
8. Adjusted vs unadjusted. ESRS, UK and EU PTD gaps are unadjusted. GRI 105 asks whether an adjusted gap was used. ILO's factor-weighted gap is not a regression-adjusted gap.
9. Gender categories. ESRS allows 'other' and 'not reported'. ISO 30414:2025 reportedly includes non-binary (unverified). The rest are binary.
10. Version changes. GRI's 405-2 ratio becomes a gap under GRI 105 once it takes effect, and ESRS numbering changed in 2026. Store the instrument version with every datapoint.

instruments.name: Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (EU) 2022/2464, as amended by the Stop-the-clock Directive (EU) 2025/794 and the Omnibus I Directive (EU) 2026/470
instruments.status: In force. Omnibus I (Directive (EU) 2026/470) published in the OJ on 26 Feb 2026 and in force since 18 Mar 2026. Member States must transpose its CSRD amendments by 19 Mar 2027. Transposition of the original CSRD is uneven: France (2023) and Italy (2024) are done; the 2026 status for Germany, Spain and the Netherlands was not re-checked.
instruments.effective: Wave 1 (large public-interest entities with more than 500 employees under the old NFRD) has reported since FY2024, with first reports in 2025. Stop-the-clock 2025/794 (April 2025) pushed wave 2 back to FY2027 and listed SMEs to FY2028. From FY2027, Omnibus I limits scope to undertakings or groups with more than 1,000 employees AND more than EUR 450m net turnover, and drops listed SMEs. Member States may exempt wave-1 companies that fall below the new thresholds for FY2025 and FY2026. Non-EU groups are covered if they have more than EUR 450m EU turnover plus an EU subsidiary or branch above EUR 200m. Assurance stays at limited level.
instruments.coverage: EU undertakings and EU parent undertakings, tested on a consolidated basis: average employees above 1,000 and net turnover above EUR 450m, both required. The counter-exception for large listed subsidiaries is deleted: a listed subsidiary included in its parent's consolidated sustainability statement is exempt from producing its own. Financial holding companies are exempt. A value-chain cap means companies with 1,000 or fewer employees cannot be asked for more than the voluntary standard (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1560).
instruments.publicAccess: Public. The sustainability statement is a section of the management report, published with the annual financial report and tagged in ESEF/XBRL. The gender metrics themselves are defined in ESRS (see EU-ESRS-2023 and EU-ESRS-2026).
interop: Defines who reports. The measures sit in ESRS (EU-ESRS-2023 for FY2024-FY2026, EU-ESRS-2026 from FY2027).
ESRS 2 Appendix B (EU-ESRS2-APPB) links ESRS datapoints to SFDR PAI and Benchmark Regulation datapoints.
Spain's LO 2/2024 requires its board-parity data to be integrated in the sustainability report.
instruments.source: Primary: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2026/470/oj and https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/oj (EUR-Lex returned empty pages to the fetch tool). Verified via https://accountancyeurope.eu/publications/omnibus-explained-key-changes-to-the-csrd-and-csddd/ , https://www.lw.com/en/insights/eu-sustainability-omnibus-published-in-the-official-journal and https://www.mofo.com/resources/insights/251222-eu-sustainability-omnibus-i-detailed-omnibus

instruments.name: European Sustainability Reporting Standards, Set 1: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772, ESRS S1 Own workforce and ESRS 2 GOV-1, as amended by the 'quick fix' Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1416
instruments.status: In force and directly applicable. The quick fix (2025/1416) was published in Nov 2025 and in force from 13 Nov 2025. Set 1 is being replaced by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563 (in force 10 Nov 2026), but stays usable for FY2026.
instruments.effective: Applies for FY2024 and FY2025 (wave 1), and optionally FY2026. For FY2026 an undertaking chooses Set 1 plus quick fix, Set 1 plus selected 2026 reliefs, or ESRS 2026 in full, and must disclose its choice. Phase-ins: undertakings with 750 or fewer employees could omit S1 entirely in their first year. Under 2025/1416, wave-1 undertakings with 750 or fewer employees may omit all of S1 for FY2025 and FY2026. Those above 750 may keep omitting only the phased-in S1 items (S1-7, S1-8 non-EEA, S1-11 to S1-15). S1-6, S1-9 and S1-16 have no phase-in above 750 employees.
instruments.coverage: CSRD reporters (see EU-CSRD). Metrics cover the undertaking's own workforce, i.e. the employees of all entities in the consolidated group, worldwide. S1 datapoints are reported only if own workforce is material (it almost always is). ESRS 2 GOV-1 is mandatory regardless of materiality.

measures.name: S1-16 §97(a) Gender pay gap (unadjusted)
measures.definition: The gender pay gap is 'the difference of average pay levels between female and male employees, expressed as percentage of the average pay level of male employees'. AR 98 formula: (average gross hourly pay of male employees minus that of female employees) divided by the male figure, times 100, including all employees. Pay follows the PTD Art. 3 definition copied into the ESRS glossary: ordinary basic or minimum wage or salary plus any other remuneration, cash or in kind, including complementary or variable components.
measures.basis: mean; gross hourly; total pay (base plus complementary/variable)
measures.population: all employees in the consolidated group, all countries
measures.period: financial year of the sustainability statement
mapsTo: SFDR PAI Table 1 #12 unadjusted gender pay gap (official: ESRS 2 Appendix B)
Benchmark Regulation Delegated Reg (EU) 2020/1816 Annex II (official: ESRS 2 Appendix B)
EU-PTD Art. 9(1)(a) (by definition: same wording; PTD leaves annual vs hourly to Member States and applies per legal employer)
EU-ESRS-2026 S1-15 §40(a) (successor)
GRI 405-2 (GRI-ESRS Interoperability Index; partial: GRI is a ratio by category and location)
UK GPG Regs 2017 reg 2(1)(a) mean hourly gap (by definition; UK counts only full-pay relevant employees and uses a snapshot pay period)
AU WGEA mean total remuneration gap (by definition; annualised FTE, not hourly)
JP women's wage as % of men's (inverse ratio, annual)

measures.name: S1-16 §97(b) Annual total remuneration ratio (not gender-specific)
measures.definition: Ratio of the annual total remuneration of the highest-paid individual to the median annual total remuneration of all employees, excluding the highest-paid individual.
mapsTo: SFDR PAI Table 3 #8 excessive CEO pay ratio (official: ESRS 2 Appendix B)
GRI 2-21 (GRI-ESRS Interoperability Index)

measures.name: S1-16 AR Gender pay gap by employee category / country (voluntary)
measures.definition: The undertaking MAY break down the gender pay gap by employee category and/or by country or segment, as context.
measures.population: employee categories chosen by the undertaking
mapsTo: EU-PTD Art. 9(1)(g) (by definition; the PTD version is mandatory and uses equal-value categories)
EU-ESRS-2026 S1-15 AR 33 adjusted gap (optional)

measures.name: S1-17 §103(a) Incidents of discrimination including harassment
measures.definition: Total number of incidents of discrimination, including harassment, reported in the period. Gender is one of the grounds; no split by gender is required.
mapsTo: SFDR PAI Table 3 #7 (official: ESRS 2 Appendix B)
GRI 406-1 (GRI-ESRS Interoperability Index)

measures.name: ESRS 2 GOV-1 §21(d) Board gender diversity
measures.definition: Percentage, by gender and other aspects of diversity, of members of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies. AR 5 says board gender diversity is calculated as an 'average ratio of female to male board members'.
measures.population: administrative, management and supervisory bodies (executive, non-executive and employee representatives)
mapsTo: SFDR PAI Table 1 #13 board gender diversity (official: ESRS 2 Appendix B)
Benchmark Regulation 2020/1816 Annex II (official: ESRS 2 Appendix B)
EU-WOB Art. 7 (by definition)
FR-BOARD, DE-FUEPOG, IT-TUF-BOARD, NL-WIQS, ES-PARIDAD (by definition)
GRI 2-9 / 405-1 (GRI-ESRS Interoperability Index)

instruments.name: Revised (simplified) ESRS: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563 (adopted 3 Jul 2026 as C(2026) 5010), replacing Annexes I and II of 2023/2772
instruments.status: Adopted 3 Jul 2026. No objection was raised during scrutiny. Published in the OJ on 21 Sep 2026, in force 10 Nov 2026. The companion voluntary standard is Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1560 (in force 24 Sep 2026).
instruments.effective: Mandatory for financial years beginning on or after 1 Jan 2027 (first reports in 2028). Optional for FY2026 once in force. Wave-2 companies newly in scope from FY2027 apply it from their first report.
instruments.coverage: CSRD reporters (see EU-CSRD). Consolidated group own workforce. Information-materiality filter applies. More than 60% of mandatory datapoints were cut.

measures.name: S1-5 §19(a) Employees by gender (headcount)
measures.definition: The total number of employees by headcount, with breakdowns by gender and by country. AR 8: reported at the end of the reporting year or as an average.
mapsTo: GRI 2-7 (by definition)

measures.name: S1-5 §19(b) Permanent and temporary employees by gender
measures.definition: Permanent employees with a breakdown by gender; temporary employees with a breakdown by gender. The gender breakdown of non-guaranteed-hours employees was removed.
mapsTo: IN BRSR permanent/other than permanent by gender (by definition)

measures.name: S1-8 §26(a) Gender distribution at top management
measures.definition: Gender distribution in number (headcount) and percentage at top management level. AR 17 defines top management as the two levels below the administrative and supervisory bodies, with flexibility to use the undertaking's own definition. Age distribution was dropped.
mapsTo: FR-RIXAIN, DE-FUEPOG §76(4), NL-WIQS subtop, ES-PARIDAD alta dirección (by definition, different populations)

measures.name: S1-14 §38 Family-related leave entitlement (no gender split)
measures.definition: Percentage of employees entitled to take family-related leave during the reporting period. AR 29: the overall percentage is sufficient. No gender breakdown and no uptake metric.
mapsTo: EU-ESRS-2023 S1-15 §93(a) (uptake-by-gender datapoint §93(b) removed)

measures.name: S1-15 §40(a) Gender pay gap (unadjusted)
measures.definition: The difference in average pay levels between female and male employees, expressed as a percentage of the average pay level of male employees. AR 31: shall include all male and female employees' gross hourly pay level. AR 32: include the ordinary basic salary and any other remuneration made available to all employees, whether in cash or in kind. AR 33: an adjusted gap by category or country is optional context. AR 34: methodology must be disclosed.
measures.basis: mean; gross hourly; base plus other remuneration (the AR 32 wording 'made available to all employees' may exclude individual discretionary pay)
measures.population: all male and female employees, consolidated
mapsTo: SFDR PAI Table 1 #12 (by definition; the Appendix B linkage in the revised set not re-verified)
EU-PTD Art. 9(1)(a) (by definition)
UK GPG reg 2(1)(a) (by definition)

measures.name: S1-15 §40(b) Annual total remuneration ratio
measures.definition: Annual total remuneration of the highest-paid individual compared with the median annual total remuneration of all employees, excluding the highest-paid individual. AR 35: base salary plus, depending on policy, cash benefits, in-kind benefits and the fair value of long-term incentives.
mapsTo: SFDR PAI Table 3 #8 (by definition)

measures.name: S1-16 §42(a) Incidents of discrimination
measures.definition: Subject to privacy rules, the number of incidents of discrimination at work on grounds including gender and racial or ethnic origin. Incidents are substantiated proceedings or registered incidents. No gender split.
mapsTo: GRI 406-1 (by definition)

instruments.name: Pay Transparency Directive (EU) 2023/970 on equal pay for equal work or work of equal value between men and women through pay transparency
instruments.status: In force since June 2023. The transposition deadline of 7 Jun 2026 has passed and most Member States missed it. On time: Italy (D.Lgs. 96/2026), Lithuania, Malta, Slovakia; Greece reported finalised later. France: bill no. 944 in the Senate (Sep 2026). Netherlands: bill 36949 before the Tweede Kamer, target 1 Jan 2027. Germany: no ministerial draft as of 25 Sep 2026. Spain: draft Royal Decree consultation May-Aug 2026. Without national law, the reporting duties do not bind private employers directly.
instruments.effective: Transposition by 7 Jun 2026. Art. 9 reporting: employers with 250 or more workers report by 7 Jun 2027 and then annually; 150-249 workers by 7 Jun 2027 and then every 3 years; 100-149 workers by 7 Jun 2031 and then every 3 years. Each report covers the previous calendar year, so 2026 data is reported in 2027. Member States may require employers under 100 to report.
instruments.coverage: Public and private employers, counted per employer (legal entity), not per group. Covers all workers with an employment contract or relationship under national law, including part-time and fixed-term. Thresholds are measured in workers.

measures.name: Art. 9(1)(a) Gender pay gap
measures.definition: Art. 3(1)(c): pay gap means the difference of average pay levels between female and male workers of an employer, expressed as a percentage of the average pay level of male workers. Art. 3(1)(a): pay is the ordinary basic or minimum wage or salary and any other consideration, cash or in kind, received directly or indirectly ('complementary or variable components'). Art. 3(1)(b): pay level is gross annual pay and the corresponding gross hourly pay.
measures.basis: mean; gross annual and/or gross hourly (Member State chooses); total pay
mapsTo: EU-ESRS-2023 S1-16 §97(a) / EU-ESRS-2026 S1-15 §40(a) (by definition: same formula; ESRS fixes hourly basis and consolidates)
IT-DLGS96 art. 9(1)(a) (transposition)
NL-PTD-BILL, FR-PTD-BILL (pending transpositions)
UK GPG Regs 2017 reg 2(1)(a) mean hourly gap (by definition)
AU WGEA average gap (by definition)
SFDR PAI #12 (by definition; hourly)

measures.name: Art. 9(1)(b) Gender pay gap in complementary or variable components
measures.definition: The mean pay gap calculated on complementary or variable components only.
measures.population: all workers (the Directive does not say whether non-recipients are included)
mapsTo: UK GPG reg 2(1)(c) mean bonus gap (by definition; UK bonus is narrower and covers 12 months to the snapshot date, recipients only)
IT-DLGS96 art. 9(1)(b)

measures.name: Art. 9(1)(c) Median gender pay gap
measures.definition: Art. 3(1)(e): the difference between the median pay level of female and the median pay level of male workers of an employer, expressed as a percentage of the male median. Art. 3(1)(d): the median pay level is the pay of the worker at which half of the employer's workers earn more and half earn less.
measures.basis: median; annual and/or hourly; total pay
mapsTo: UK GPG reg 2(1)(b) median hourly gap (by definition)
AU WGEA median total remuneration gap (by definition)
IT-DLGS96 art. 9(1)(c)
No ESRS equivalent (ESRS has the mean only)

measures.name: Art. 9(1)(d) Median gender pay gap in complementary or variable components
measures.definition: The median gap computed on complementary or variable components.
mapsTo: UK GPG reg 2(1)(d) median bonus gap (by definition)
IT-DLGS96 art. 9(1)(d)

measures.name: Art. 9(1)(e) Proportion of female and male workers receiving complementary or variable components
measures.definition: The share of female workers, and separately of male workers, who receive any complementary or variable component.
mapsTo: UK GPG reg 2(1)(e) proportion receiving bonus (by definition)
IT-DLGS96 art. 9(1)(e)

measures.name: Art. 9(1)(f) Proportion of female and male workers in each quartile pay band
measures.definition: Art. 3(1)(f): a pay quartile band is each of four equal groups into which workers are divided by pay level, from lowest to highest. The share of women and of men in each band is reported.
measures.basis: headcount; ranked by pay level (annual or hourly)
mapsTo: UK GPG reg 2(1)(f) quartile pay bands (by definition; UK ranks by hourly pay of full-pay employees)
AU WGEA quartiles (by definition)
IT-DLGS96 art. 9(1)(f)

measures.name: Art. 9(1)(g) Gender pay gap by categories of workers, split into basic and complementary/variable pay
measures.definition: The gender pay gap between workers by categories of workers, broken down by ordinary basic wage or salary and by complementary or variable components. Art. 3(1)(h): a category of workers is those doing the same work or work of equal value, grouped non-arbitrarily on gender-neutral criteria (skills, effort, responsibility, working conditions).
mapsTo: ES-REGISTRO RD 902/2020 art. 6 equal-value register (by definition)
FR-INDEX indicator 1 (looks alike: age x CSP groups, FTE annual, with tolerance)
IT-ART46 pay by category (by definition)
EU-ESRS-2023 S1-16 AR breakdown (voluntary)
IT-DLGS96 art. 9(1)(g)

measures.name: Art. 10 Joint pay assessment trigger
measures.definition: A joint pay assessment with workers' representatives is required where pay reporting shows a difference in average pay level of at least 5% between female and male workers in any category of workers that is not justified on objective, gender-neutral criteria and not remedied within six months.
mapsTo: ES Estatuto de los Trabajadores art. 28.3 / RD 902 art. 6: 25% justification threshold (different threshold)
FR-INDEX below-75 points corrective measures (different mechanism)
IT-DLGS96 art. 10 (transposition)

instruments.publicAccess: Indicators (a)-(f) go to the national monitoring body, which publishes them so employers, sectors and regions can be compared. Employers may also publish on their website. Member States may compile (a)-(f) themselves from tax or social-security data. Indicator (g) goes to workers, their representatives and the monitoring body, and to the labour inspectorate and equality body on request; it is not public.
interop: The ESRS glossary copies the PTD definitions of 'pay' and 'pay level'.
Indicators (a)-(f) mirror the UK GPG Regs 2017 reg 2(1)(a)-(f) in structure.
National transpositions: IT-DLGS96, NL-PTD-BILL, FR-PTD-BILL

instruments.name: Women on Boards Directive (EU) 2022/2381 on improving the gender balance among directors of listed companies
instruments.status: In force (OJ 7 Dec 2022). Transposition was due 28 Dec 2024. The target date of 30 Jun 2026 has now passed. Art. 12 lets Member States that already had 30%/25% outcomes or equally effective laws before 27 Dec 2022 suspend parts of the regime; FR, DE, IT and NL rely on pre-existing quotas, and ES transposed through LO 2/2024. The Directive expires at the end of 2038.
instruments.effective: Objectives apply from 30 Jun 2026. Annual reporting applies from transposition.
instruments.coverage: Companies with their registered office in a Member State whose shares trade on an EU regulated market. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises are excluded (fewer than 250 employees and turnover up to EUR 50m or balance sheet up to EUR 43m).

measures.name: Art. 5(1)(a) Under-represented sex among non-executive directors
measures.definition: Members of the under-represented sex hold at least 40% of non-executive director positions by 30 Jun 2026. The required number is the one closest to 40% without exceeding 49% (Annex).
measures.population: non-executive directors (supervisory board in two-tier systems)
measures.period: status at each reporting date; target 30 Jun 2026
mapsTo: ESRS 2 GOV-1 §21(d) (by definition)
SFDR PAI #13 (by definition)
DE-FUEPOG AktG §96(2) 30%, NL-WIQS one-third, FR-BOARD 40%, IT-TUF-BOARD two-fifths, ES-PARIDAD 40% (national equivalents)

measures.name: Art. 5(1)(b) Under-represented sex among all directors
measures.definition: Alternative objective chosen by the Member State: at least 33% of all director positions, executive and non-executive, held by the under-represented sex.
mapsTo: ESRS 2 GOV-1 §21(d) (by definition)

measures.name: Art. 5(2) Individual quantitative objectives for executive directors
measures.definition: Listed companies under the 40% non-executive route set individual quantitative objectives to improve gender balance among executive directors.
mapsTo: DE-FUEPOG §76(3a) AktG minimum one woman on the Vorstand (by definition)
NL-WIQS streefcijfers (by definition)

measures.name: Art. 7 Annual gender representation report
measures.definition: Once a year, listed companies report to the competent authorities on gender representation on their boards, distinguishing non-executive and executive directors, and on measures taken towards the Art. 5 objectives. They publish this on their website. If the objectives are missed, they give reasons and describe the measures.
mapsTo: ESRS 2 GOV-1 §21(d) (by definition)
ES-PARIDAD art. 529 bis (transposition)

instruments.publicAccess: Public, on the company website. National authorities publish lists of companies meeting the objectives.
interop: Its board metric overlaps ESRS 2 GOV-1 and SFDR PAI #13, but WoB distinguishes NED and ED and frames the target as the under-represented sex.

instruments.status: In force since 1 Jan 2023. A Commission proposal to revise SFDR (late 2025) is pending; its effect on entity-level PAI was not verified.
instruments.effective: PAI statements are published annually by 30 June for the previous calendar year.
instruments.coverage: Financial market participants with more than 500 employees must publish PAI statements; others comply or explain. The figures are aggregated from investee companies.

measures.name: PAI Table 1 #12 Unadjusted gender pay gap
measures.definition: Average unadjusted gender pay gap of investee companies. The unadjusted gender pay gap is the difference between average gross hourly earnings of male and of female paid employees, as a percentage of male average gross hourly earnings.
mapsTo: EU-ESRS-2023 S1-16 §97(a) (official: ESRS 2 Appendix B)
EU-PTD 9(1)(a) (by definition)

measures.name: PAI Table 1 #13 Board gender diversity
measures.definition: Average ratio of female to male board members in investee companies, expressed as a percentage of all board members. Board means the administrative, management or supervisory body.
mapsTo: ESRS 2 GOV-1 §21(d) (official: ESRS 2 Appendix B)
EU-WOB Art. 7 (by definition)

instruments.name: Index de l'égalité professionnelle femmes-hommes (Code du travail L.1142-8 to L.1142-10, D.1142-2 et seq.; loi n° 2018-771 'Avenir professionnel')
instruments.status: In force. Still due by 1 Mar 2027 (covering 2026). Bill no. 944 would replace it with PTD indicators from about 2028.
instruments.coverage: Companies and UES (unités économiques et sociales) with 50 or more employees. Five indicators for more than 250 employees; four for 50-250. Computed per legal entity or UES, not per listed group.

measures.name: Indicator 1: Écart de rémunération (40 points)
measures.definition: Gap in average pay, reconstituted as full-time equivalent, between women and men within groups of 4 age bands (under 30, 30-39, 40-49, 50+) crossed with CSP (socio-professional category) or classification level. A group counts only with at least 3 women and 3 men, and covered staff must be at least 40% of the total. A relevance threshold of 5% (CSP) or 2% (levels) is deducted. Groups are weighted by headcount and the absolute value is taken. Included: base pay, individual and collective bonuses, paid-leave pay. Excluded: overtime, seniority bonus, profit-sharing, equity, severance, shift premiums. A 0% gap scores 40 points; above 20% scores 0.
measures.basis: mean; annual gross FTE; partly adjusted (by group, after tolerance)
measures.population: employees present at least 6 months in the period, excluding apprentices, professionalisation contracts, temps, expatriates and those absent more than 6 months
measures.period: 12 consecutive months ending in the previous year
mapsTo: EU-PTD 9(1)(g) (looks alike: grouped gap, but not equal-value categories)
EU-ESRS-2023 S1-16 (not equivalent: adjusted, FTE-annual, absolute value)
FR-PTD-BILL category indicator (successor)

measures.name: Indicator 2: Écart de taux d'augmentations individuelles (20 points; 35 points for 50-250 employees including promotions)
measures.definition: Difference, in percentage points, between the share of women and the share of men receiving an individual raise. For more than 250 employees: by CSP, excluding promotions, at least 10 women and 10 men per CSP. For 50-250 employees: company level, including promotions, and the better of the points or headcount method.
mapsTo: No EU or ESRS equivalent

measures.name: Indicator 3: Écart de taux de promotions (15 points, more than 250 employees)
measures.definition: Difference in promotion rates (moving to a higher level or coefficient) between women and men, by CSP.
mapsTo: IT-ART46 promotions by sex (by definition)

measures.name: Indicator 4: Retour de congé maternité (15 points)
measures.definition: Share of women returning from maternity or adoption leave who received the raise required by the catch-up obligation. 100% earns 15 points; anything less earns 0.
mapsTo: EU-ESRS-2023 S1-15 (not equivalent)

measures.name: Indicator 5: Dix plus hautes rémunérations (10 points)
measures.definition: Number of employees of the under-represented sex among the 10 highest-paid employees. 4-5 earns 10 points, 2-3 earns 5, 0-1 earns 0.
mapsTo: UK GPG upper quartile share (looks alike)
EU-PTD 9(1)(f) top quartile (looks alike)

measures.name: Index total score (/100)
measures.definition: Sum of the indicator points, prorated if some indicators cannot be calculated; the Index is not calculable if fewer than 75 points are achievable. Below 75: corrective measures within 3 years. Below 85: progress objectives.
mapsTo: No equivalent elsewhere

instruments.publicAccess: Public. Published on the company website by 1 March and kept until the next year. Declared on Egapro, where the ministry makes it searchable ('Consulter l'index'). Sent to the CSE (works council).
interop: Being replaced by the PTD-based indicators in FR-PTD-BILL
instruments.quote: 'au plus tard le 1er mars' (Egapro, publication deadline)

instruments.name: Loi n° 2021-1774 du 24 décembre 2021 (loi Rixain): balanced representation in senior management (Code du travail L.1142-11 to L.1142-13)
instruments.status: In force. The 30% obligation applies from 1 Mar 2026; 40% from 1 Mar 2029.
instruments.effective: Gaps published since 1 Mar 2022/2023. 30% quota from 1 Mar 2026; 40% from 1 Mar 2029, with 2 years to comply before a financial penalty.
instruments.coverage: Companies employing at least 1,000 employees for the third consecutive year (entity level).

measures.name: Share of women and men among cadres dirigeants
measures.definition: Percentage of each sex among senior executives (cadres dirigeants, Code du travail L.3111-2). Target: at least 30% of each sex from 2026, 40% from 2029.
mapsTo: EU-ESRS-2023 S1-9 §66(a) / EU-ESRS-2026 S1-8 (by definition; different population)
ES-PARIDAD alta dirección (by definition)

measures.name: Share of women and men among members of instances dirigeantes

areas.notes:
State as of 12 Oct 2026.

INTEROPERABLE (built on the same definition)
1. Gender pay gap. The PTD Art. 3/9(1)(a), ESRS S1-16 §97(a) (S1-15 §40(a) in ESRS 2026) and SFDR PAI #12 all use the formula (male average minus female average) divided by the male average. The ESRS glossary copies the PTD's definitions of 'pay' and 'pay level'. ESRS 2 Appendix B is the official link from S1-16 to SFDR PAI #12 and the Benchmark Regulation. Italy's D.Lgs. 96/2026 copies the PTD wording.
2. Board gender diversity. ESRS 2 GOV-1 §21(d) maps officially to SFDR PAI #13 (Appendix B). The WoB Directive Art. 7 matches by definition.
3. Structure. PTD indicators (a)-(f) parallel the UK GPG Regs reg 2(1)(a)-(f): mean and median gap, variable-pay gaps, share receiving variable pay, and quartiles.
4. GRI mapping. The GRI-ESRS Interoperability Index maps S1-6, S1-9, S1-13, S1-15, S1-16 and S1-17 to GRI 2-7, 405-1, 404-1/404-3, 401-3, 405-2/2-21 and 406-1. There is no ISSB counterpart for S1.

LOOKS ALIKE BUT IS NOT THE SAME
- France's Index indicator 1 is adjusted. It is an FTE-annual mean gap within age-band by CSP groups, with a 5%/2% tolerance, reported as an absolute value and converted to points. It cannot be compared with an unadjusted gap.
- Spain's registro retributivo has mean and median by pay component and job classification, but it is entity-level and not public. Its trigger is 25%; the PTD's is 5%.
- Spain's EINF 'brecha salarial' has no prescribed method.
- Germany's EntgTranspG report contains only headcounts by sex, with no pay figure. Its §11 median is an individual comparator, not a published metric.
- Italy's art. 46 report gives total pay by category for each biennium, and is not public.
- Japan reports women's pay as a percentage of men's (a ratio, annual). Australia's WGEA uses annualised FTE pay with a median headline.
- Top management means different things. ESRS Set 1 uses one and two levels below the board; ESRS 2026 uses two levels with flexibility. France (Rixain) uses cadres dirigeants and executive committees. Germany uses the two levels below the Vorstand, as targets only. The Netherlands' subtop is company-defined. Spain uses alta dirección.
- Board measures differ. The WoB Directive counts the under-represented sex and splits NED from ED. ESRS AR 5 says 'average ratio of female to male', while SFDR says '% of all board members'. France excludes employee directors from its 40% count. Germany's 30% includes employee representatives.

TRAPS
- Hourly vs annual. ESRS, SFDR and the UK use hourly pay. The PTD defines pay level as both annual and hourly and leaves the choice to Member States; Italy keeps both. France uses FTE-annual; Japan uses annual.
- Mean vs median. ESRS has the mean only. The PTD, UK and Spain report both. France uses the mean. Australia's headline is the median.
- Base vs total pay. The PTD covers all pay. Italy narrows 'livello retributivo' to fixed, continuing pay and excludes individual discretionary or temporary pay, which is a likely gap against the Directive. ESRS 2026 AR 32 counts 'remuneration made available to all employees'. France's Index excludes overtime, profit-sharing, equity and seniority pay.
- Permanent vs all staff. The PTD covers all workers. The Netherlands adds agency workers in a separate section. France's Index excludes apprentices, temps, expatriates, people absent more than 6 months and people present less than 6 months. The UK counts full-pay employees only. ESRS counts employees, not non-employees, and adds an 'other' gender category.
- Snapshot and period. The PTD uses the previous calendar year, reported by 7 June. ESRS uses the financial year, with headcount at year end or as an average. France uses 12 months, published by 1 March. The Netherlands' SER figures are at financial-year end. Germany uses the last year of a 3- or 5-year cycle. The UK snapshot is 5 April or 31 March.
- Reporting entity vs listed group. CSRD/ESRS figures are consolidated across the group worldwide. PTD and national regimes work per legal employer in each country; Italy lets a group with one pay policy aggregate nationally, and France allows the UES level. Since Omnibus I, a listed subsidiary covered by its parent's consolidated report may publish no S1 data of its own.
- Materiality and phase-ins. S1 data appears only if own workforce is material. Wave-1 companies with 750 or fewer employees may omit S1 entirely for FY2024-FY2026.
- Version breaks. For FY2026 companies choose Set 1 or ESRS 2026. Numbering shifts (S1-16 becomes S1-15, S1-9 becomes S1-8, S1-6 becomes S1-5). Gender splits for training, family leave, disability and non-guaranteed-hours staff are dropped, which breaks time series.
- Sign and rounding. Japan's measure is an inverse ratio. France reports the absolute gap. The WoB Directive and Spain cap at 49%; Germany rounds to whole persons.

TIMING
- First PTD reports are due in June 2027, but only where the Directive is transposed: Italy, Lithuania, Malta, Slovakia and probably Greece.
- France's Index is still due 1 Mar 2027.
- The Netherlands' first reports are due June 2028, covering 2027.
- Germany had no draft as of 25 Sep 2026. Spain's draft Royal Decree was in consultation from May to August 2026.
- ESRS 2026 is mandatory from FY2027. The CSRD scope of more than 1,000 employees and EUR 450m applies from FY2027.

VERIFICATION LIMITS
- EUR-Lex returned empty pages to the fetch tool. The quotes for the PTD, ESRS Set 1, WoB and SFDR come from the official texts as known, cross-checked against Italy's verbatim transposition and EFRAG pages, but were not re-fetched.
- ESRS 2026 paragraph numbers follow EFRAG's December 2025 technical advice. The Commission's final text (2026/1563) reportedly differs in a number of areas (one analysis counts 13), so check paragraph numbers against the OJ.
