instruments.name: Equality Act 2010 (Gender Pay Gap Information) Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/172)
instruments.jurisdiction: United Kingdom - Great Britain (England, Scotland, Wales); not Northern Ireland
instruments.status: In force. Made under s.78 Equality Act 2010. GOV.UK guidance updated 21 May 2026: 'men' and 'women' now means biological sex, following For Women Scotland v Scottish Ministers [2025] UKSC 16. The rules are unchanged. Voluntary action plans have been added on the same service from 2026 (see UK-ERA2025-S33). Outsourced-provider information (s.34 ERA 2025) is enacted but not yet in force.
instruments.effective: In force 6 April 2017. Annual snapshot date 5 April (first one 5 April 2017). Publish within 12 months, so by 4 April of the next year (first deadline 4 April 2018). Current cycle: snapshot 5 April 2026, deadline 4 April 2027.
instruments.coverage: Private and voluntary-sector employers, plus public bodies not listed in Schedule 2 of SI 2017/353, with 250 or more relevant employees on the snapshot date. Headcount, not FTE. Each legal entity reports separately; group figures are optional extras. Multiple payrolls in one entity are merged. Agency workers count at the agency. Partners and LLP members are excluded. Employers below 250 may report voluntarily.

measures.name: Mean gender pay gap in hourly pay
measures.definition: Reg 2(1)(a): the difference between the mean hourly rate of pay of male full-pay relevant employees and that of female full-pay relevant employees. Formula: (male mean - female mean) / male mean x 100. A positive figure means women are paid less.
measures.basis: Hourly. Mean. Pay = ordinary pay (basic pay, allowances, piecework, pay for leave, shift premium) plus any bonus paid in the snapshot pay period (pro-rated to that period). Gross, after salary sacrifice. Excludes overtime, redundancy or termination pay, pay in lieu of leave, expenses and benefits in kind. Converted to a weekly figure (x 7 / days in the pay period), then divided by weekly working hours. Hours come from the contract, or a 12-week average for variable hours.
measures.population: Full-pay relevant employees of the legal entity on the snapshot date. Includes part-time, job-share, temporary, casual, zero-hours, apprentices and personally-contracted self-employed workers. Excludes anyone on reduced or nil pay because of leave (for example maternity leave on statutory pay, or long-term sick leave). Headcount. Biological sex. No permanent/temporary split and no split by level.
measures.period: The pay period that contains 5 April
mapsTo: UK-GPG-PUB-2017 mean hourly gap: identical by definition (only the snapshot date differs: 31 March)
UK-ERDB-EDPG mean ethnicity and disability hourly gaps: same calculation (official, GOV.UK consultation response, March 2026)
UK-NI-EA2016-S19 proposed mean gap: intended to mirror GB (by definition, regulations not yet made)
UK-SCOT-PSED-2012 average hourly pay gap: looks alike only (excludes overtime, no full-pay filter, every 2 years)

EU Pay Transparency Directive Art 9(1)(a) gender pay gap: by definition, partial (EU 'pay level' is gross annual pay and the corresponding gross hourly pay, including complementary or variable components)
ESRS S1-16 / SFDR PAI 12 unadjusted gender pay gap: by definition, partial (average gross hourly pay)
Australia WGEA mean total remuneration gap: looks alike only (annualised FTE total remuneration including superannuation)
Japan Women's Participation Act wage difference: looks alike only (women's annual average wage as % of men's, not adjusted for hours, inverse sign)
India BRSR P5 EI3 median remuneration by gender: looks alike only (annual, median, by board/KMP/employees/workers)

measures.name: Median gender pay gap in hourly pay
measures.definition: Reg 2(1)(b): the difference between the median hourly rate of pay of male and female full-pay relevant employees. Formula: (male median - female median) / male median x 100.
measures.basis: Hourly. Median. Same pay definition as the mean measure.
measures.population: Full-pay relevant employees (as for the mean measure)
measures.period: The pay period that contains 5 April
mapsTo: UK-GPG-PUB-2017 median hourly gap: identical by definition
UK-ERDB-EDPG median gaps: same calculation (official, March 2026 response)
EU Pay Transparency Directive Art 9(1)(c) median gender pay gap: by definition, partial
Australia WGEA median total remuneration gap: looks alike only (annualised FTE)
India BRSR P5 EI3 median remuneration: looks alike only (reports levels, not a gap; annual)

measures.name: Mean bonus gender pay gap
measures.definition: Reg 2(1)(c): the difference between the mean bonus pay paid to male relevant employees and that paid to female relevant employees. The mean for each sex = total bonus paid to that sex / number of that sex who received a bonus. Formula: (male - female) / male x 100.
measures.basis: Bonus pay in money, vouchers, securities or options that relates to profit-sharing, productivity, performance, incentive or commission, plus monetary long-service awards. Not pro-rated. Mean taken over recipients only. Excludes overtime, redundancy pay, loans and benefits in kind.
measures.population: All relevant employees who received a bonus. The full-pay filter does not apply.
mapsTo: UK-GPG-PUB-2017: identical by definition
UK-ERDB-EDPG: same calculation (official)
EU Pay Transparency Directive Art 9(1)(b) gap in complementary or variable components: by definition, partial (EU components are wider than 'bonus')

measures.name: Median bonus gender pay gap
measures.definition: Reg 2(1)(d): the difference between the median bonus pay paid to male and female relevant employees, taken over recipients only. Formula: (male median - female median) / male median x 100.
measures.basis: Bonus pay as for the mean bonus measure. Median.
measures.population: All relevant employees who received a bonus
mapsTo: UK-GPG-PUB-2017: identical by definition
UK-ERDB-EDPG: same calculation (official)
EU Pay Transparency Directive Art 9(1)(d): by definition, partial

measures.name: Proportion of men and women receiving bonus pay
measures.definition: Reg 2(1)(e): the proportions of male and female relevant employees who were paid bonus pay. Calculated as (men receiving a bonus / all male relevant employees) x 100, and the same for women.
mapsTo: UK-GPG-PUB-2017: identical by definition
UK-ERDB-EDPG: same calculation (official)
EU Pay Transparency Directive Art 9(1)(e) proportion receiving complementary or variable components: by definition, partial

measures.name: Proportion of men and women in each pay quartile
measures.definition: Reg 2(1)(f): the proportions of male and female full-pay relevant employees in the lower, lower middle, upper middle and upper quartile pay bands. Employees are ranked by hourly pay and split into four bands of equal headcount. Employees with the same pay are spread so the sex mix is the same in each band they span.
measures.unit: % men and % women within each of 4 bands (8 figures)
measures.basis: Hourly pay, as for the mean and median measures
measures.period: The pay period that contains 5 April
mapsTo: UK-GPG-PUB-2017: identical by definition
UK-ERDB-EDPG: same calculation (official)
EU Pay Transparency Directive Art 9(1)(f) quartile pay bands: by definition, partial
Australia WGEA quartile composition: looks alike only (annualised FTE total remuneration)

measures.name: Written statement of accuracy
measures.definition: A statement confirming the information is accurate, signed by an appropriate person (director, designated member, partner or equivalent). Its name appears in the ResponsiblePerson field.
measures.population: Private and voluntary-sector employers (most public authorities are exempt)
mapsTo: UK-ERA2025-S33 action plan 'responsible person': same role (official, GOV.UK action plan guidance)

measures.name: Supporting narrative and website link
measures.definition: Optional explanation of the figures and planned actions, plus a link to the employer's own publication
mapsTo: UK-ERA2025-S33 action plan: replaces informal narrative from 2027 (by definition)

instruments.publicAccess: Public. Data is entered on the GOV.UK gender pay gap service (gender-pay-gap.service.gov.uk) and published on the employer's own website for at least 3 years. Data can be searched by employer and downloaded as CSV by reporting year (2017-18 onward) under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Columns include EmployerName, CompanyNumber, SicCodes, DiffMeanHourlyPercent, DiffMedianHourlyPercent, DiffMeanBonusPercent, DiffMedianBonusPercent, Male/FemaleBonusPercent, quartile shares by sex, EmployerSize, ResponsiblePerson, DueDate, DateSubmitted and SubmittedAfterTheDeadline. Enforced by the EHRC.
interop: GOV.UK 'Gender pay gap reporting: guidance for employers' (updated 21 May 2026): one methodology for both private (SI 2017/172) and public (SI 2017/353) employers; only the snapshot dates differ
GOV.UK consultation response on mandatory ethnicity and disability pay gap reporting (March 2026): the same 6 measures, snapshot dates, online service and enforcement will be reused
GOV.UK 'Creating an action plan: guidance for employers' (April 2026): action plans are published alongside GPG data on the same service
instruments.quote: the difference between the mean hourly rate of pay of male full-pay relevant employees

instruments.name: Equality Act 2010 (Specific Duties and Public Authorities) Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/353), Schedule 1 - public-sector gender pay gap information
instruments.jurisdiction: United Kingdom - England, plus non-devolved and cross-border authorities listed in Schedule 2
instruments.status: In force (part of the public sector equality duty specific duties). GOV.UK guidance on biological sex (21 May 2026) applies here too.
instruments.effective: In force 31 March 2017. Annual snapshot date 31 March. Publish within 12 months, so by 30 March of the next year (current cycle: snapshot 31 March 2026, deadline 30 March 2027).
instruments.coverage: Public authorities listed in Schedule 2 with 250 or more employees on the snapshot date. These include most government departments and arm's-length bodies, local authorities, NHS bodies, universities, and most schools, academies and multi-academy trusts. Public bodies not in Schedule 2 report under SI 2017/172 with a 5 April snapshot. Scottish and Welsh devolved authorities follow their own rules.

measures.name: Mean hourly pay gap
measures.definition: Same as SI 2017/172 reg 2(1)(a): the difference in mean hourly pay of male and female full-pay relevant employees, as % of the male figure
measures.basis: Hourly, mean, same ordinary-pay plus pro-rated-bonus definition
measures.population: Full-pay relevant employees of the authority
measures.period: The pay period that contains 31 March
mapsTo: UK-GPG-2017 mean hourly gap: identical by definition (official: single GOV.UK methodology); snapshot 31 March vs 5 April

measures.name: Median hourly pay gap
measures.period: The pay period that contains 31 March
mapsTo: UK-GPG-2017 median hourly gap: identical by definition

measures.name: Mean bonus gap
measures.definition: As SI 2017/172 reg 2(1)(c), taken over recipients
measures.basis: Bonus pay, mean over recipients, not pro-rated
measures.population: All relevant employees who received a bonus
mapsTo: UK-GPG-2017 mean bonus gap: identical by definition

measures.name: Median bonus gap
measures.population: All relevant employees who received a bonus
mapsTo: UK-GPG-2017 median bonus gap: identical by definition

measures.name: Bonus proportions by sex
mapsTo: UK-GPG-2017 bonus proportions: identical by definition

measures.name: Quartile pay band composition
measures.unit: % men and % women in each of 4 bands
measures.period: The pay period that contains 31 March
mapsTo: UK-GPG-2017 quartiles: identical by definition

instruments.publicAccess: Public. Published on the GOV.UK gender pay gap service, in the same CSV files as private employers, and on the authority's own website. Most public authorities do not file a written statement.
interop: GOV.UK 'When to report' guidance: 31 March snapshot and 30 March deadline for Schedule 2 authorities; 5 April and 4 April for everyone else
GOV.UK 'Making your calculations': one calculation method for both regimes
instruments.quote: 31 March for most public authority employers

instruments.name: Equality Act 2010 (Specific Duties) (Scotland) Regulations 2012 (SSI 2012/162), regs 7-8, as amended by SSI 2016/159
instruments.jurisdiction: United Kingdom - Scotland (devolved public authorities only)
instruments.status: In force. The 2016 amendment lowered the threshold from 150 to 20 employees and revised the publication timings (new reg 8A).
instruments.effective: Pay gap published by 30 April 2013 and every second year after that. Equal pay statements every 4 years. The 2016 amendment changed timings and threshold from 2017.
instruments.coverage: Scottish listed public authorities with 20 or more employees. Does not cover companies; included only for completeness of the public-sector picture.

measures.name: Gender pay gap (Scottish PSED)
measures.definition: Reg 7: the percentage difference among the authority's employees between men's average hourly pay (excluding overtime) and women's average hourly pay (excluding overtime)
measures.basis: Hourly, 'average' (mean is usual, not defined in the regulation), excludes overtime
measures.population: All employees of the authority (no full-pay filter)
measures.period: Most recent available data. Published every 2 years.
mapsTo: UK-GPG-PUB-2017 mean hourly gap: looks alike only (no full-pay filter, different timing, 'average' undefined) - by definition

measures.name: Equal pay statement and occupational segregation
measures.definition: Reg 8: a statement on equal pay policy and occupational segregation between men and women (later extended to race and disability)
mapsTo: No equivalent in GB company regimes (by definition)

instruments.publicAccess: Public, on each authority's own website. Not on the GOV.UK service.
interop: GOV.UK GPG guidance 'Who needs to report': Scottish and Welsh public authorities have different rules
instruments.quote: men's average hourly pay (excluding overtime) and women's average hourly pay (excluding overtime)

instruments.name: Employment Act (Northern Ireland) 2016, section 19 (gender pay and disclosure of information) and the planned Gender Pay Gap Information Regulations (Northern Ireland)
instruments.status: Passed but not in force. Section 19 was enacted in 2016 and has never been commenced. The Department for Communities consulted from 25 November 2024 to 14 February 2025 and published its response with final policy proposals on 7 October 2025. Draft regulations are expected after the Good Jobs Employment Rights Bill receives Royal Assent. I found no evidence that any have been laid as of October 2026.
instruments.effective: Not in force. Commentators expect regulations in 2027 at the earliest, a first snapshot in 2027 and first reports in 2028 (not confirmed).
instruments.coverage: Proposed: public, private and voluntary employers with 250 or more employees (the threshold was still under review). Ethnicity and disability reporting has been set aside for now. The Equality Commission for Northern Ireland would enforce.

measures.name: Gender pay gap information (proposed)
measures.definition: S.19 requires employers to publish information on differences in pay between male and female employees, with methodology set by regulations. Policy is to broadly mirror the GB six measures (mean, median, bonus and quartiles) on an annual snapshot.
measures.basis: Expected hourly, mean and median, as in GB (not final)
mapsTo: UK-GPG-2017 six measures: intended mirror (by definition, policy statement only)

measures.name: Action plan to eliminate pay differences
measures.definition: Where there are pay differences between men and women, s.19 requires the employer to publish an action plan to eliminate them (detail left to regulations)
mapsTo: UK-ERA2025-S33 equality action plan: similar concept (by definition)

instruments.publicAccess: Not yet applicable
interop: DfC departmental response (7 October 2025): framework broadly mirrors GB reporting
Advocacy groups (Human Rights Consortium) argue NI must also track the EU Pay Transparency Directive under the Windsor Framework. This is not an official position.
instruments.quote: The public consultation took place between 25 November 2024 and 14 February 2025.

instruments.name: Employment Rights Act 2025, section 33 (new s.78A Equality Act 2010: equality action plans) and GOV.UK 'Creating an action plan: guidance for employers'
instruments.status: Passed. The Act received Royal Assent on 18 December 2025. Section 33 is an enabling power and is still prospective (not commenced). A voluntary scheme has run since 6 April 2026 under GOV.UK guidance (list of 18 actions published 4 March 2026, step-by-step guidance 7 April 2026). Plans become mandatory only once regulations are made. As of September 2026 these were still to be drafted, with further consultation and penalties expected.
instruments.effective: Voluntary for the 2026-27 reporting year: publish with GPG data by 4 April 2027 (30 March for public bodies). Mandatory from spring or April 2027, subject to regulations not yet made. Plans can be required no more often than every 12 months.
instruments.coverage: Employers with 250 or more employees. One plan per legal entity with 250 or more employees. Smaller employers are encouraged to take part.

measures.name: Gender pay gap action(s)
measures.definition: At least one action, chosen from the government's evidence-based list (recruitment, development and promotion, diversity, transparency), to address the employer's gender pay gap
mapsTo: UK-NI-EA2016-S19 action plan: similar concept (by definition)
UK-ERDB-EDPG ethnicity and disability action plans: the government intends a single equality action plan covering sex, race and disability (official, March 2026 response)
EU Pay Transparency Directive Art 10 joint pay assessment: looks alike only (EU duty is triggered by an unexplained gap of 5% or more)
Japan Women's Participation Act general employer action plan: similar concept (by definition)

measures.name: Menopause support action(s)
measures.definition: At least one action supporting employees experiencing menopause (including perimenopause), taking account of intersectional needs and workforce demographics
mapsTo: No equivalent in other UK regimes (by definition)

measures.name: Responsible person
measures.definition: Name of the director, partner or senior officer responsible, for private and voluntary-sector employers
mapsTo: UK-GPG-2017 written statement signatory (by definition)

instruments.publicAccess: Public. Plans are created, submitted and published on the gender pay gap service alongside the employer's GPG data.
interop: GOV.UK 'Creating an action plan: guidance for employers' (overview) and 'Action plans: list of actions' collection
GOV.UK GPG guidance, Overview and 'Closing your gender pay gap' (updated April and May 2026), links action plans to GPG reporting
GOV.UK ethnicity and disability pay gap response (March 2026): aim of one equality action plan
instruments.quote: Subject to legislation, these will become mandatory from spring 2027.

instruments.name: Employment Rights Act 2025, section 34 (provision of information relating to outsourced workers; new subsection in s.78 Equality Act 2010)
instruments.status: Passed (Royal Assent 18 December 2025) but prospective, so not in force. It needs regulations. Implementation is tied to the wider pay gap reforms in the Equality (Race and Disability) Bill, and no date has been set.
instruments.effective: Not in force, no date set
instruments.coverage: Employers subject to the s.78 gender pay gap regulations (250 or more employees)

measures.name: Identity of outsourced or contract-worker service providers
measures.definition: Regulations may require GPG reporters to identify the providers or employers of workers supplied under outsourcing contracts. This is not a requirement to report those workers' pay (Lewis Silkin, September 2026).
measures.population: Outsourced or contract workers (outside the 'relevant employee' headcount)
mapsTo: No equivalent elsewhere in the UK; partly addresses the gap where outsourced low-paid staff fall outside UK-GPG-2017 (by definition)

instruments.publicAccess: Expected to be on the gender pay gap service. Not yet applicable.
interop: EHRC parliamentary briefing on the Employment Rights Bill describes it as a power to require information on outsourced service providers
instruments.quote: Provision of information relating to outsourced workers

instruments.name: Equality (Race and Disability) Bill - mandatory ethnicity and disability pay gap reporting (government consultation response with indicative draft clauses, March 2026)
instruments.jurisdiction: United Kingdom - Great Britain (will not apply in Northern Ireland)
instruments.status: Proposed. Policy was confirmed in the March 2026 consultation response (857 responses; consultation ran 18 March to 10 June 2025), with indicative clauses in Annex A. The Bill has not been published or introduced. Commentators say it was not in the 2026 King's Speech and expect publication in 2027.
instruments.effective: Not in force. Pinsent Masons (September 2026) says a first snapshot is unlikely before April 2028, with reporting from 2029.
instruments.coverage: Employers with 250 or more employees in GB. Additional public-body reporting proposals (by grade, recruitment, retention, progression) were dropped in favour of voluntary guidance.

measures.name: Ethnicity pay gap - same 6 measures
measures.definition: Mean and median hourly pay gaps, mean and median bonus gaps, bonus proportions and quartile composition. Minimum comparison is binary: White (including White Other) vs all other ethnic groups combined. Comparisons across the 5 broad ONS groups apply where thresholds are met. The minimum group size (at least 10 per quarter has been floated) is still under policy work.
measures.basis: Hourly and bonus, mean and median, as in GPG
measures.population: Relevant employees and full-pay relevant employees, as in GPG
measures.period: Same snapshot dates as GPG (5 April / 31 March)
mapsTo: UK-GPG-2017 six measures: same calculations, dates and service (official, March 2026 response)
UK-FCA-UKLR-DIV board minority-ethnic target: looks alike only (FCA uses ONS categories; workforce vs board)

measures.name: Disability pay gap - same 6 measures
measures.definition: Binary disabled vs non-disabled comparison using the Equality Act 2010 definition of disability
mapsTo: UK-GPG-2017 six measures: same calculations (official)

measures.name: Workforce composition and declaration rates
measures.definition: Workforce make-up by ethnicity and disability, and the share of employees who have declared that data
mapsTo: UK-CA2006-S414C employee counts by sex: looks alike only (sex, year-end, quoted companies)

measures.name: Ethnicity and disability action plans
measures.definition: Large employers must take action on ethnicity and disability pay gaps, aligned with gender and menopause plans and aiming at one equality action plan
mapsTo: UK-ERA2025-S33 (official alignment intent)

instruments.publicAccess: Planned: the same online service as GPG, so public
interop: GOV.UK 'Consultation on mandatory ethnicity and disability pay gap reporting: government response' (March 2026): same reporting dates, online service, 6 measures and enforcement as GPG
Final stage impact assessment (published with the response)
instruments.quote: report the same 6 measures for ethnicity and disability pay gap reporting

instruments.name: FCA UK Listing Rules UKLR 6.6.6R(9)-(11) and UKLR 6 Annex 1R (board and executive management diversity, from PS22/3), with DTR 7.2.8AR diversity policy
instruments.jurisdiction: United Kingdom (applies to UK and overseas issuers listed in London)
instruments.status: In force. Created by PS22/3 (published 20 April 2022) as LR 9.8.6R(9)-(11) and LR 14.3.33R, then carried into the UKLR from 29 July 2024. UKLR 6.6.6R was last amended 28 March 2025. The Handbook shows a future version dated 1 January 2027, linked to the PS26/19 sustainability changes; I could not confirm whether (9)-(11) change. The FCA had said it would review the rules after 3 years; I found no published outcome. A DTR review is under way (per the DBT September 2026 consultation).
instruments.effective: Financial years starting on or after 1 April 2022. UKLR numbering from 29 July 2024.
instruments.coverage: Issuers with equity shares (or certificates representing them) in the commercial companies category (UKLR 6). Parallel provisions with their own Annex 1 tables apply in other share categories (for example UKLR 22.2.30R). PS22/3 scope covered closed-ended investment funds and sovereign controlled companies, and excluded open-ended investment companies, shell companies and debt issuers. DTR 7.2.8AR applies to issuers that must publish a corporate governance statement.

measures.name: Board target: at least 40% women (comply or explain)
measures.definition: UKLR 6.6.6R(9)(a)(i): a statement of whether, as at a chosen reference date within the accounting period, at least 40% of the individuals on the board of directors are women. If not met, the company states the reasons.
measures.basis: Board headcount (executive and non-executive directors together)
measures.population: Board of directors of the listed company
measures.period: A chosen reference date within the accounting period. Any change from the prior year must be explained, and board changes between the reference date and report approval must be disclosed.
mapsTo: UK-FTSE-WLR 40% women on boards: same threshold (by definition; FCA targets were set to match the FTSE Women Leaders Review per PS22/3; WLR uses its own reference date)
UK-CA2006-S414C directors by sex: same population, but counts at financial year end (by definition)
EU Women on Boards Directive 2022/2381: looks alike only (40% of non-executive directors, or 33% of all directors)
ESRS GOV-1 / SFDR PAI 13 board gender diversity: by definition, partial
India Companies Act s.149 / SEBI LODR Reg 17: looks alike only (at least one woman director, no %)
Australia ASX Corporate Governance Principles Rec 1.5: looks alike only (measurable objective, 30% for the S&P/ASX 300)

measures.name: Board target: a woman in at least one senior board position
measures.definition: UKLR 6.6.6R(9)(a)(ii): at least one of chair, chief executive, senior independent director or chief financial officer is a woman
mapsTo: UK-FTSE-WLR key-roles recommendation: looks alike only (WLR: Chair or SID on the board and/or CEO or FD; FCA counts any of the four)

measures.name: Board target: at least one director from a minority ethnic background
measures.definition: UKLR 6.6.6R(9)(a)(iii), using ONS categories excluding White groups. Not a gender measure; listed for completeness.
mapsTo: UK-ERDB-EDPG binary ethnicity split: looks alike only

measures.name: Annex 1 Table 1 - board by gender identity or sex
measures.definition: UKLR 6.6.6R(10): 'Number of board members' and 'Percentage of the board' for Men, Women, optional [Other categories], and 'Not specified/ prefer not to say'. The company chooses whether to report sex or gender identity and must explain its approach.
measures.basis: Headcount. Sex or gender identity, at the company's choice.
mapsTo: UK-CA2006-S414C(8)(c)(i) directors by sex: by definition (counts; year-end vs reference date; sex vs gender identity)
UK-FTSE-WLR board %: by definition
Japan annual securities report female officer ratio: by definition, partial

measures.name: Annex 1 Table 1 - senior board positions by gender
measures.definition: 'Number of senior positions on the board (CEO, CFO, SID and chair)' held by men, women and so on
mapsTo: UK-FTSE-WLR women in Chair, SID, CEO and FD roles: by definition

measures.name: Annex 1 Table 1 - executive management by gender identity or sex
measures.definition: 'Number in executive management' and 'Percentage of executive management'. Executive management (FCA glossary) = the executive committee or most senior executive or managerial body below the board, or if there is none, the most senior managers reporting to the CEO. Includes the company secretary; excludes administrative and support staff.
measures.population: Executive management (directors who sit on the executive committee also appear here)
mapsTo: UK-FTSE-WLR women on the Executive Committee: by definition; WLR 'Leadership' also adds direct reports, so it looks alike only
UK-CGC2024-P23 senior management and direct reports: looks alike only
UK-CA2006-S414C(8)(c)(ii) senior managers: looks alike only (function-based and includes subsidiary directors; FRC says the two can differ)
India BRSR KMP by gender: looks alike only (statutory KMP)
Australia WGEA CEO/KMP manager categories: looks alike only

measures.name: Data collection approach
measures.definition: UKLR 6.6.6R(11): explanation of how the data for (9) and (10) was collected, applied consistently to all individuals (6.6.15G). Overseas data protection limits may be explained (6.6.13R).
mapsTo: No direct equivalent (by definition)

measures.name: Board diversity policy (DTR 7.2.8AR)
measures.definition: Corporate governance statement must describe the diversity policy for the administrative, management and supervisory bodies (and, since PS22/3, the audit, remuneration and nomination committees), covering aspects such as gender, with objectives, implementation and results, or explain why there is none
mapsTo: UK-CGC2024-P23 diversity and inclusion policy narrative: overlapping (by definition)

instruments.publicAccess: Public. Included in the annual financial report (published and filed on the National Storage Mechanism). No central structured dataset.
interop: FCA PS22/3 (April 2022): targets set by reference to the FTSE Women Leaders Review (gender) and the Parker Review (ethnicity); ONS ethnicity categories

DBT 'Modernising corporate reporting' consultation (7 September to 30 November 2026): says the Listing Rules contain similar and overlapping requirements to the s.414C sex breakdown, which it proposes to remove
FRC UK Corporate Governance Code pages: senior management definitions differ between the Code (also used for Hampton-Alexander reporting) and s.414C
instruments.quote: at least 40% of the individuals on its board of directors are women

instruments.name: Companies Act 2006, s.414C(8)(c) - strategic report breakdown by sex (quoted companies), inserted by SI 2013/1970
instruments.status: In force. Its removal is proposed in the DBT 'Modernising corporate reporting' consultation (published 7 September 2026, closes 30 November 2026; outcome expected within about 6 months), which cites overlap with the FCA Listing Rules. The proposal would also remove CEO pay ratios. Not yet changed.
instruments.effective: Since 1 October 2013 (financial years ending on or after 30 September 2013)
instruments.coverage: Quoted companies: UK-incorporated companies whose equity is officially listed in the UK or an EEA state, or admitted to dealing on NYSE or Nasdaq. Covers the company, or the group in a group strategic report.

measures.name: Directors by sex
measures.definition: s.414C(8)(c)(i): the number of persons of each sex who were directors of the company, at the end of the financial year (the parent company in a group report)
mapsTo: UK-FCA-UKLR-DIV Table 1 board: same population (by definition); FCA uses a reference date and allows gender identity
UK-FTSE-WLR board: by definition

measures.name: Senior managers by sex
measures.definition: s.414C(8)(c)(ii): the number of persons of each sex who were senior managers, excluding directors. A senior manager is an employee responsible for planning, directing or controlling the activities of the company or a strategically significant part of it. areas.notes:
UK state as of 12 October 2026.

What lines up:
- The private-sector regulations (SI 2017/172) and the public-sector Schedule 1 (SI 2017/353) use the same six measures and the same GOV.UK method and service. Only the snapshot and deadline differ: 5 April / 4 April for private employers, 31 March / 30 March for most public bodies. These can share one schema.
- Ethnicity and disability pay gaps will reuse the same six calculations, dates and service. This is official, from the March 2026 government response. The Bill has not been introduced, and a first snapshot is unlikely before April 2028.
- Action plans will sit on the same service. They are voluntary since April 2026 and due to become mandatory in 2027, but the regulations do not exist yet.
- The FCA 40% board target and the FTSE Women Leaders Review 40% board target share a threshold. PS22/3 set the FCA targets to match the Review.
- The s.414C directors-by-sex count matches FCA Table 1 if the FCA reference date is the year end.

What only looks alike:
- FCA "executive management" is the executive committee only.
- Women Leaders Review "Leadership" and Code Provision 23 both cover the executive committee plus direct reports.
- s.414C "senior managers" is a function-based definition and includes subsidiary directors. The FRC says these figures can differ.
- The FCA senior-role target counts any of Chair, CEO, SID or CFO. The Review asks for a woman as Chair or SID and/or as CEO or FD.
- Scotland's public-sector measure is an "average hourly pay excluding overtime" figure every two years, with no full-pay filter.
- UK SRS (ISSB) has no gender metric. It cannot be mapped to anything.

Traps:
1. Hourly vs annual. The UK gap is hourly, based on one pay period with any bonus paid in it pro-rated. Australia's WGEA uses annualised full-time-equivalent pay, Japan an annual average not adjusted for hours, and India's BRSR annual medians. The EU Pay Transparency Directive defines pay as both gross annual and hourly.
2. Mean vs median. The UK reports both. The bonus mean and median are taken over people who received a bonus only, so a small bonus gap can sit next to a large gap in who gets a bonus.
3. Base vs total. "Ordinary pay" includes allowances and shift premium and excludes overtime and benefits in kind. Bonus is reported separately over 12 months. There is no base-only gap.
4. Who is counted. The hourly and quartile measures use full-pay relevant employees only, which drops people on reduced leave pay such as maternity leave. The bonus measures use all relevant employees. "Relevant employees" include temporary, zero-hours and personally contracted workers, and exclude partners and agency staff. There is no permanent vs non-permanent split, unlike Japan and India.
5. Snapshot dates. GOV.UK labels a year such as "2025-26" for a 5 April 2025 snapshot. The FCA uses a reference date the company chooses within its accounting period. s.414C uses the financial year end. The Review uses 31 October.
6. Reporting entity vs listed group. Pay gap reports are filed per GB legal entity with 250 or more employees, so a FTSE group may file several reports or none, and overseas staff are missing. Group totals are voluntary. Link filings to groups through the CompanyNumber field. FCA, s.414C and the Review report at company or group level.
7. Sex vs gender identity. Pay gap reports use biological sex (GOV.UK guidance of 21 May 2026, after For Women Scotland [2025] UKSC 16). The FCA lets companies report sex or gender identity, with a "not specified" row.
8. Sign. The UK gap is (men - women) / men. Japan reports women's pay as a percentage of men's.

Pending changes:
- The Employment Rights Act 2025 section on outsourced-worker information (s.34) is enacted but not in force.
- Northern Ireland: s.19 of the Employment Act (NI) 2016 has never been commenced; regulations are pending.
- The DBT consultation (closes 30 November 2026) proposes removing the s.414C sex breakdown.
- I found nothing repealed or struck down in this area.

Limits:
- legislation.gov.uk returned empty pages to the fetch tool. Statutory wording therefore comes from GOV.UK guidance and search-result extracts of legislation.gov.uk.
- The web-search budget ran out before I could check: any FCA 3-year review of the diversity rules, whether the 1 January 2027 version of UKLR 6.6.6R changes paragraphs (9) to (11), the exact text of DTR 7.2.8AR, and the Welsh public-sector duties (SI 2011/1064, not included).
- I did not save anything on purpose. The fetch tool cached one GOV.UK PDF (equality-action-plans-and-outsourcing-factsheet.pdf) in the session tool-results folder. I did not read it.

instruments.name: Workplace Gender Equality Act 2012 (Cth), as amended by the Workplace Gender Equality Amendment (Closing the Gender Pay Gap) Act 2023 and the Workplace Gender Equality Amendment (Setting Gender Equality Targets) Act 2025 (current compilation C2025C00286, Comp. No. 23)
instruments.status: In force. The current compilation took effect on 4 April 2025. A further amendment has passed but is not yet in force: Regulatory Reform Omnibus Act 2026 (No. 87, 2026) Sch 1 Pt 7 received assent on 18 Sep 2026 and commences on 1 Jan 2027 (see AU-RROA-2026-PT7). Nothing has been repealed or struck down. The register shows no amendment after the 2025 Targets Act other than the Omnibus Act.
instruments.effective: Originally the Affirmative Action (Equal Employment Opportunity for Women) Act 1986. It was renamed the WGE Act by the Equal Opportunity for Women in the Workplace Amendment Act 2012 (assent 6 Dec 2012). The Respect at Work Act 2022 amendments apply from 13 Dec 2022. The Closing the Gender Pay Gap amendments commenced on 12 Apr 2023: s 15A pay-gap publication applies to reporting periods starting on or after 1 Apr 2022 (non-Commonwealth employers) and 1 Jan 2023 (Commonwealth). It also added s 16C (CEO must give the WGEA Executive Summary and Industry Benchmark Report to the board) and GEI 6 on sexual harassment. The Targets amendments commenced on 4 Apr 2025 (ss 4A, 13(3AA)-(3AC), 17A-17C).
instruments.coverage: A 'relevant employer' is a non-public-sector employer with 100 or more employees in Australia (s 4). This includes companies, NFPs, higher education providers and, since 2022, Commonwealth public sector employers; state and territory governments are excluded. Corporate groups count the combined Australian employees of the parent and its subsidiaries. A 'designated relevant employer' (DRE) employs 500 or more employees at any time (s 4A(1)) and stops being one after 6 continuous months below 400 (s 4A(2)); WGEA applies the DRE test to each employing ABN's direct employees. The reporting period is 1 April to 31 March (s 13A), and the public report is due within 2 months of period end, i.e. 31 May, with extensions to 31 July (s 13B). Headcount includes full-time, part-time, casual and fixed-term staff and excludes contractors and agency workers.

measures.name: Public report on the six gender equality indicators (GEIs)
measures.definition: s 3(1) lists the 'gender equality indicators': (a) gender composition of the workforce; (b) gender composition of governing bodies of relevant employers; (c) equal remuneration between women and men; (d) availability and utility of flexible working arrangements and arrangements supporting employees with family or caring responsibilities; (e) consultation with employees on gender equality issues in the workplace; (ea) sexual harassment, harassment on the ground of sex or discrimination; (f) other matters the Minister specifies. s 13(1): each reporting period a relevant employer 'must prepare a public report in writing containing information relating to the employer' and the GEIs, covering the matters the Minister specifies (see AU-WGEA-GEI-INSTR-2023).
measures.unit: Structured report (employee-level workforce file plus questionnaire)
measures.basis: Set by the GEI Matters Instrument
measures.population: All employees of the relevant employer in Australia
measures.period: Reporting period 1 April to 31 March; workforce data at an employer-chosen snapshot date within that period
mapsTo: ASX CGPR 4th ed. Rec 1.5(c)(3)(B): a listed 'relevant employer' may disclose its most recent GEIs instead of its own proportions (official equivalence)
ASX draft 5th ed. (Jul 2026): the workforce and senior-executive diversity recommendation is removed 'in light of' WGE Act reporting (official cross-reference)

measures.name: Employer remuneration gender equality performance (s 15A publication)
measures.definition: s 15A(1): the Agency must publish, for each relevant employer and reporting period, aggregate information 'showing the employer's performance and progress in achieving gender equality in relation to remuneration'. It must not disclose personal information or any individual's remuneration (s 15A(4)). WGEA implements this as employer gender pay gaps (see AU-WGEA-GPG-PUB).
measures.unit: % gaps and quartile shares (published by WGEA)
measures.basis: Set by WGEA methodology: annualised full-time equivalent (FTE) pay, mean and median, base salary and total remuneration
measures.population: Relevant employers reporting 80 or more employees
mapsTo: See the AU-WGEA-GPG-PUB measures

measures.name: Gender equality target outcome (DREs)
measures.definition: s 17C: a DRE is 'taken to fail to comply with this Act if, at the end of a target cycle', without reasonable excuse, it has not either 'met the target' or 'demonstrated improvement against the target' in the final-year public report compared with the baseline report, for each selected target.
measures.unit: Met / improved / not met, for each of 3 targets
measures.population: DREs (each employing ABN with 500 or more direct employees)
measures.period: 3-year target cycle; the first private-sector cycle runs over the 2026-27 to 2028-29 reporting periods
mapsTo: No equivalent outside Australia (the EU PTD Art 10 joint pay assessment only looks alike: it is a remediation trigger, not a chosen target)

instruments.publicAccess: WGEA may publish public reports (s 15), but not until 28 days after on-time lodgement. Remuneration information is not published (s 14) except as s 15A aggregates. Personal information is withheld (s 13C). Employers must tell employees and shareholders how to access their report (s 16) and notify unions within 7 days (s 16A). Data is free on the WGEA Data Explorer (wgea.gov.au/data-statistics/data-explorer). Non-compliant employers can be named (s 19D) and become ineligible for Commonwealth procurement.
interop: ASX CGPR 4th ed. Rec 1.5(c)(3)(B) explicitly accepts 'the entity's most recent "Gender Equality Indicators", as defined in and published under that Act'
ASX draft 5th ed. (21 Jul 2026) drops the workforce diversity recommendation because of WGE Act reporting
WGEA notes that ABS national pay-gap figures (full-time base, AWOTE) are not directly comparable with WGEA employer gaps
instruments.quote: an employer of 100 or more employees in Australia

instruments.name: Workplace Gender Equality (Matters in relation to Gender Equality Indicators) Instrument 2023 (F2023L00085), as amended by the Amendment Instrument 2025 (F2025L00472); current compilation F2025C00430
instruments.status: In force. Registered 5 Feb 2023, remaking the 2013 instrument. Amended with effect from 4 Apr 2025; that amending instrument was itself automatically repealed in Oct 2025 once spent. Sunsets 1 Apr 2033.
instruments.effective: Applies from the 2023-24 reporting period, with CEO/head-of-business pay mandatory from 2024 lodgement. The 2025 amendments apply to reporting periods commencing after 4 Apr 2025, i.e. from 1 Apr 2026 for the private sector (s 13). They added definitions of 'Agency' and 'family and domestic violence', replaced the 'non-manager' definition, replaced s 8(1)(a) per-employee fields, and changed s 9(n)-(o) wording. WGEA practice: year of birth is mandatory from 2026 lodgement, and occupation codes move from ANZSCO to OSCA for the 2027 program.
instruments.coverage: All relevant employers (100 or more employees in Australia), at employing-ABN level, rolled into corporate or submission groups

measures.name: Workforce gender composition (GEI 1)
measures.definition: s 6: workforce data broken down by gender, employment status, year of birth, primary workplace location, and manager or non-manager. 'Manager' includes the CEO or equivalent, key management personnel (KMP) and other managers. 'Non-manager' is any other employee, e.g. professionals, technicians and trades, clerical, sales, machinery operators, labourers, graduates, apprentices (s 5). 'Employment status' is full-time, part-time, permanent/ongoing, casual or fixed-term (s 5).
measures.unit: Headcount and % women / men (non-binary collected but excluded from pay-gap figures)
measures.basis: Headcount (not FTE) of employees on the snapshot date
measures.population: All employees in Australia: full-time, part-time, casual and fixed-term, including those on parental or extended leave. Excludes contractors, directors without employment contracts, agency workers, and staff overseas for more than 6 months of the period.
measures.period: Snapshot date chosen by the employer anywhere in 1 Apr to 31 Mar (WGEA recommends 31 Dec), the same for all employees in one file
mapsTo: ASX CGPR 4th ed. Rec 1.5(c)(3)(A) 'proportions of men and women ... across the whole workforce' (official substitution via 1.5(c)(3)(B))
ESRS S1-6 employees by gender, headcount (by definition; ESRS is group-wide, WGEA is Australia only)
India SEBI BRSR Section A employees and workers by gender (by definition; BRSR splits permanent and other-than-permanent)
GRI 405-1(b) (by definition)

measures.name: Women in management by manager category (GEI 1)
measures.definition: Gender composition of managers in each category: CEO or equivalent, KMP, and other managers. In WGEA's Workplace Profile the categories are CEO, KMP, other executives/general managers, senior managers and other managers.
mapsTo: ASX CGPR 4th ed. Rec 1.5 'senior executive positions' (looks alike: ASX lets each entity define 'senior executive', and covers the group worldwide)
ESRS S1-9 gender distribution at top management (looks alike: one and two levels below the administrative bodies)
Japan female manager ratio under the Women's Participation Act and annual securities report (looks alike: Japanese 'kanrishoku' differs from WGEA manager categories)
BRSR KMP by gender (looks alike)

measures.name: Appointments, promotions and resignations by gender (GEI 1)
measures.definition: s 6: applicants appointed, by gender and manager or non-manager; promotions and resignations by number and proportion, by gender, employment status and manager or non-manager
mapsTo: BRSR Section A turnover rate by gender, permanent employees and workers (looks alike)
ESRS S1-6 turnover (looks alike; not required by gender)
GRI 401-1 (by definition)

measures.name: Governing body gender composition (GEI 2)
measures.definition: s 7: whether the employer has a governing body; if so, the number of members and of chairs by gender; any gender composition target set for the body; and any policy or strategy on its gender composition. From 2026 WGEA accepts one governing body per ABN.
measures.unit: Headcount and % women members and chairs; yes/no for target and policy
measures.population: Governing body (board) of each employing ABN in the group, not only the listed parent
measures.period: As reported for the reporting period
mapsTo: ASX CGPR 4th ed. Rec 1.5 board proportions and S&P/ASX 300 30% objective (official substitution via 1.5(c)(3)(B))
UK FCA UKLR board diversity targets (by definition)
EU Women on Boards Directive 2022/2381 (by definition)
ESRS 2 GOV-1 board gender diversity (by definition)
SEBI LODR women-director requirement and BRSR representation of women on the board (by definition)

measures.name: Employee-level remuneration data (GEI 3 input)
measures.definition: s 8(1)(a): for each employee except 'key management personnel with a reporting distance above the Chief Executive Officer or equivalent', report gender, employment status, year of birth, location, manager or non-manager, and enough information to work out annualised full-time equivalent remuneration. WGEA Workplace Profile: 'Base salary' is mandatory and is 'actual annual earnings before tax in full-time and full-year equivalent amounts'. It includes ordinary wages, leave and leave loading, employer-funded parental leave, penalty rates within ordinary hours and salary-sacrificed amounts. 'Total remuneration' is mandatory and must be at least base salary. It adds superannuation, bonuses (pro-rated or fixed), overtime outside expected hours, short- and long-term incentives, fringe benefits, allowances, commissions, share allocations and cashed-out leave.
measures.basis: Annualised (part-year grossed up to a full year) and FTE (part-time and casual grossed up to full-time hours); casuals use their actual hourly rate; gross pre-tax; base and total
measures.population: All employees on the snapshot date, including the CEO (from 2024 lodgement); excludes KMP who sit above the CEO
measures.period: Pay over the 12 months to the snapshot date
mapsTo: Input for the WGEA published gaps (AU-WGEA-GPG-PUB); not published per employee (s 14)

measures.name: Equal remuneration policy and gender pay gap analysis (GEI 3)
measures.definition: s 8(1)(b)-(d): whether the employer has an equal remuneration policy or strategy; 'whether any gender remuneration gap analysis has been undertaken and, if so, when'; and the actions taken as a result
mapsTo: EU PTD Art 10 joint pay assessment (looks alike: there it is mandatory when an unexplained gap is 5% or more)
GRI 2-21 / 405-2 (looks alike)

measures.name: Flexible work, parental leave, carer and family-and-domestic-violence supports (GEI 4)
measures.definition: s 9: availability and use of flexible working arrangements, and supports for employees with family and caring responsibilities. This includes employer-funded paid parental leave and its uptake by gender, and family and domestic violence support (s 9(n)-(o), 'family and domestic violence' as defined in the Fair Work Act 2009).
mapsTo: ESRS S1-15 family-related leave (by definition)
BRSR Principle 3 parental leave return and retention by gender (looks alike)
Japan men's childcare-leave uptake disclosure (looks alike)

measures.name: Employee consultation on gender equality (GEI 5)
measures.definition: s 10: whether, how and with whom the employer consulted employees on gender equality issues
mapsTo: No quantified equivalent elsewhere

measures.name: Sexual harassment, harassment on the ground of sex, or discrimination (GEI 6)
measures.definition: s 11: policies or strategies, training, and processes for preventing and responding to sexual harassment, sex-based harassment and discrimination (inserted by the 2023 Act)
mapsTo: BRSR Principle 5 sexual harassment complaint counts (looks alike: counts, not policies)
ESRS S1-17 incidents (looks alike)

instruments.publicAccess: Non-personal, non-remuneration public report content is published per employer on the WGEA Data Explorer and in public datasets. Employee-level pay is never published. Employers receive a confidential Executive Summary and Industry Benchmark Report, which the CEO must give to the board (s 16C).
interop: Its GEI content is what ASX Rec 1.5(c)(3)(B) accepts in place of entity-defined proportions
Occupation coding follows the ABS ANZSCO, moving to OSCA from the 2027 program
instruments.quote: whether any gender remuneration gap analysis has been undertaken and, if so, when

instruments.name: WGEA employer gender pay gap publication (made under WGE Act s 15A; method in the WGEA Reporting Guide 'Calculating gender pay gaps' and the Private Sector Employer Gender Pay Gap Technical Guide 2024)
instruments.status: Operational, published every year. 27 Feb 2024: first release (2022-23 data), medians only, excluding CEO, head-of-business (HOB) and casual-manager pay. 4 Mar 2025: 2023-24 data, adding averages and including CEO, HOB and casual managers. 3 Mar 2026: 2024-25 data, with private and Commonwealth public sector released together for the first time (about 8,500 employers and 1,600 corporate groups).
instruments.effective: Publication duty from 12 Apr 2023, applying to reporting periods starting on or after 1 Apr 2022
instruments.coverage: Gaps are published for 'all relevant employers who report 80 or more employees'. For corporate groups they are published at group level and for each ABN in the group with more than 80 employees; smaller ABNs are counted in group figures only.

measures.name: Median total remuneration gender pay gap
measures.definition: 'Gender pay gap = 100 X (Median total remuneration of men – Median total remuneration of women) / Median total remuneration of men'. The median is the middle employee when all are ordered from lowest to highest earnings; with an even count it is the average of the two middle employees. WGEA's headline employer measure.
measures.unit: % of men's median; a positive figure means men are paid more; one decimal place; WGEA's target range is -5% to +5%
measures.basis: Annualised FTE total remuneration (base plus superannuation, bonuses, overtime, allowances, incentives and other benefits); median
measures.population: All full-time, part-time and casual employees in Australia on the snapshot date, including CEO/equivalent, HOBs and casual managers (from 2023-24 data). Excludes non-binary employees, overseas reporting managers and zero-income employees.
measures.period: Employees on the employer-chosen snapshot date (1 Apr to 31 Mar); pay over the 12 months to that date; labelled by reporting period (e.g. '2024-25', published Mar 2026)
mapsTo: EU Pay Transparency Directive 2023/970 Art 9(1)(c) median gender pay gap (by definition: same (M-W)/M formula, pay includes complementary components; EU defines 'pay level' as gross annual and corresponding gross hourly pay)
UK GPG Regs 2017 reg 2(1)(b) median hourly pay gap (looks alike: hourly ordinary pay, which excludes overtime and employer pension; full-pay relevant employees only; 5 April snapshot)
India SEBI BRSR Principle 5 EI 3(a) median remuneration by gender (looks alike: actual annual pay, not FTE; shown as amounts for board, KMP, employees and workers)
WGEA Targets Instrument s 12 baseline (official, same value)

measures.name: Median base salary gender pay gap
measures.definition: The same formula using median annualised FTE base salary. Base salary is ordinary wages or salary, including leave pay and penalty rates within ordinary hours, and excluding super, bonuses and overtime.
measures.population: As for the median total remuneration gap
measures.period: As for the median total remuneration gap
mapsTo: EU PTD Art 9(1)(g) gap by category of workers, ordinary basic wage (looks alike: EU reports it by worker category)
GRI 405-2 basic salary ratio (looks alike: a women-to-men ratio by employee category and location)
WGEA Targets s 12 baseline (official)

measures.name: Average (mean) total remuneration gender pay gap
measures.definition: '(average male total remuneration – average female total remuneration) / average male total remuneration' x 100. Published from the 2025 release (2023-24 data) onwards.
measures.population: As for the median total remuneration gap; including CEO pay raises the mean
measures.period: As for the median total remuneration gap
mapsTo: EU PTD Art 9(1)(a) gender pay gap (by definition)
ESRS S1-16 gender pay gap, difference of average pay levels as % of male average, on gross hourly pay (by definition, but ESRS is hourly and group-wide)
UK GPG Regs 2017 reg 2(1)(a) mean hourly pay gap (looks alike)
Japan Women's Participation Act wage difference (looks alike: women's average annual wage as % of men's, so it is the complement of a gap; split into all, regular and non-regular workers)
GRI 405-2 remuneration ratio (looks alike)
WGEA Targets s 12 baseline (official)

EU PTD Art 9(1)(g) basic-pay gap by category (looks alike)
WGEA Targets s 12 baseline (official)

measures.definition: Employees are sorted by total remuneration from lowest to highest and split into four groups of equal size (upper, upper middle, lower middle, lowest). WGEA publishes the % women and % men in each quartile (Technical Guide, as summarised by WGEA; the Guide PDF itself was not opened).

EU PTD Art 9(1)(f) and Art 3 'pay quartile band', four equal groups by pay level (by definition)

instruments.publicAccess: Free and public on the WGEA Data Explorer and in the annual Employer Gender Pay Gaps Report. An employer may add a voluntary Employer Statement, which is linked next to its results. WGEA has no bonus-gap or bonus-receipt measures, so UK reg 2(1)(c)-(e) and EU Art 9(1)(b),(d),(e) have no Australian counterpart; the difference between the base and total gaps is the only proxy.

WGEA notes its employer gaps differ from the ABS national gap (full-time adult ordinary-time base earnings)

instruments.name: Workplace Gender Equality (Gender Equality Targets) Instrument 2025 (F2025L00473), made under WGE Act s 17B, with WGE Act ss 4A, 13(3AA)-(3AC) and 17A-17C
instruments.status: In force since 4 Apr 2025. Private-sector DREs made their first selection in the 2025-26 report lodged 1 Apr to 31 May 2026. The structure of the cycles changes from 1 Jan 2027 under the Omnibus Act 2026 (passed, not yet in force).
instruments.effective: 4 April 2025, immediately after the Targets Act commenced. First cycle: baseline is the 2024-25 reporting period (Commonwealth public sector: calendar 2024). Targets are selected in 2026 and run over three reporting periods (2026-27 to 2028-29), assessed in the final-year report. From 1 Jan 2027: 3-year cycles, with the next cycle starting 4 years after the last (a 12-month window); the baseline is the report for the period ending 12 months before the cycle starts; existing cycles continue.
instruments.coverage: DREs only: each employing ABN that directly employs 500 or more employees in Australia. A parent or subsidiary that reaches 500 only when combined with others in its group is not a DRE. Each DRE in a group selects its own targets.

measures.name: Reduce the gender pay gap (numeric, s 12)
measures.definition: The employer picks one value (the average or median of base salary, or the average or median of total remuneration) and must 'nominate the reduction (as a percentage) in the difference in the specified value between employees of each gender' against the baseline. WGEA validates the reduction to one decimal place as a percentage-point change; keeping the baseline value is not allowed. A gap already at zero cannot be selected.
measures.unit: Percentage-point reduction in the WGEA gap
measures.basis: Employer's choice of the four WGEA gap measures (mean or median; base or total)
measures.population: All employees of the ABN (WGEA gap population)
measures.period: Baseline report vs final year of the 3-year cycle
mapsTo: AU-WGEA-GPG-PUB mean/median base/total gaps (official, same value)
No target regime elsewhere (EU PTD Art 10 5% trigger looks alike)

measures.name: Reduce the gender pay gap for managers or non-managers (numeric, s 13)
measures.definition: The employer specifies managers or non-managers and either the average or median of total remuneration (base salary is not an option), then nominates a percentage reduction against the baseline. Only the selected figure is published.
measures.basis: Total remuneration; mean or median; annualised FTE
measures.population: Managers (CEO, KMP, other managers) or non-managers
mapsTo: BRSR Principle 5 EI 3(a) median remuneration for KMP vs other employees (looks alike)
EU PTD Art 9(1)(g) gap by worker category (looks alike)

measures.name: Increase representation of the under-represented gender (numeric, ss 7-10)
measures.definition: Increase the share of the gender under-represented in the baseline among non-managers (s 7), managers in a specified category, which may be all managers (s 8), promotions to manager (s 9), or a specified pay quartile (s 10). The employer nominates the increase as a percentage.
mapsTo: AU-WGEA-GEI-INSTR-2023 GEI 1 measures (official)
AU-WGEA-GPG-PUB quartile composition (official)

measures.definition: Nominate the percentage increase in representation of the gender under-represented on the governing body in the baseline
mapsTo: ASX CGPR Rec 1.5 / draft Rec 2.3(c) board objective (by definition)

measures.definition: The menu has 19 items, 9 numeric and 10 action, and custom targets are not allowed. Beyond the above it includes: undertake a gender pay gap analysis (s 14); equal remuneration and pay equity policies (s 15); introduce or improve employer-funded parental leave (ss 16, 18); increase primary parental leave uptake by the under-represented gender (s 17); carer supports (s 19); flexible work (s 20); proportion of managers who are part-time (s 21); family and domestic violence supports (s 22); employee consultation (s 23); sexual harassment policies and reporting to the CEO, KMP and governing body (ss 24-25). mapsTo: By definition, the GEI 3-6 items in AU-WGEA-GEI-INSTR-2023

Not meeting or improving every target without reasonable excuse is non-compliance, which can lead to naming (s 19D) and loss of eligibility for Commonwealth procurement.

areas.notes:
INTEROPERABLE (official). (1) ASX Rec 1.5(c)(3)(B) lets an ASX-listed 'relevant employer' disclose its WGEA Gender Equality Indicators instead of its own men/women proportions. This is the only official cross-walk found. (2) The ASX draft 5th edition (21 Jul 2026, consultation closed 14 Sep) removes the workforce and senior-executive gender recommendation and leaves that reporting to the WGE Act. It keeps a 30% women / 30% men board objective for the S&P/ASX 300 and is proposed for financial years from 1 Jul 2027. (3) The pay-gap and representation targets in the WGEA Targets Instrument use exactly the WGEA published measures as baselines. I found no official mapping between WGEA measures and the UK GPG Regulations, the EU Pay Transparency Directive (PTD), ESRS, SEBI BRSR, Japan or GRI. Every cross-regime link in mapsTo is 'by definition' or 'looks alike'.

CLOSE BY DEFINITION. WGEA mean and median total-remuneration gaps use the same (M-W)/M formula as EU PTD Art 9(1)(a)/(c) and ESRS S1-16. WGEA quartiles (four equal groups ranked by pay) match EU Art 3 'pay quartile band' and UK reg 2(1)(f) in concept. Board % women is the same concept in WGEA GEI 2, ASX 1.5, UK UKLR, EU WoB, ESRS GOV-1 and BRSR.

ONLY LOOKS ALIKE. UK mean/median hourly gaps use ordinary pay, which excludes overtime and employer pension, cover full-pay relevant employees only, and use a 5 April snapshot. BRSR gives median remuneration as amounts, actual annual pay (not FTE), for board, KMP, employees and workers. Japan reports women's mean wage as a % of men's (the complement of a gap), split into all, regular and non-regular workers. GRI 405-2 is a women-to-men ratio by employee category and location. ASX 'senior executive' (defined by each entity), WGEA manager categories (CEO down to 'other managers'), ESRS 'top management' and Japan's kanrishoku are not the same population. WGEA has no bonus gap or bonus-receipt measures, so UK reg 2(1)(c)-(e) and EU Art 9(1)(b),(d),(e) have no Australian counterpart.

TRAPS.
- Hourly vs annual: WGEA is annualised AND full-time-equivalent, so it is an hours-neutral pay rate. It is closer to UK and EU hourly measures than to BRSR or Japan actual annual pay. But casuals' FTE figures include the casual loading, full-time hours differ by award, and total remuneration includes overtime.
- Mean vs median: the 2024 release (2022-23 data) was median-only and excluded CEO, HOB and casual-manager pay. Means and executive pay arrived in the 2025 release (2023-24), which is a series break. WGEA's national figure (about 21% private-sector average total remuneration) and the ABS 11.5% (full-time adult ordinary-time base earnings) are different measures, and neither is an employer gap.
- Base vs total: WGEA total remuneration includes employer superannuation (12% guarantee from 1 Jul 2025), bonuses, incentives, share allocations and fringe benefits. WGEA base salary includes leave pay and penalty rates within ordinary hours.
- Permanent vs all staff: WGEA covers all full-time, part-time, casual and fixed-term employees in Australia. It excludes non-binary employees, overseas reporting managers, zero-income staff, contractors and staff overseas for more than 6 months. BRSR splits permanent from other staff and Japan splits regular from non-regular.
- Snapshot date: each employer picks any date from 1 Apr to 31 Mar (31 Dec is recommended). Pay is the 12 months to that date, so '2024-25' data can mean calendar-2024 pay, published Mar 2026, a lag of about 15 months. Commonwealth public sector employers move to April periods from 1 Jan 2027 under the Omnibus Act.
- Reporting entity vs listed group: WGEA works at employing-ABN level, rolled up to corporate or submission groups, Australian employees only. Gaps are published for the group and for each ABN with more than 80 employees. The 500-employee DRE test (targets and standards) is per ABN, so a large group split across smaller ABNs may have no targets. ASX disclosures cover the listed group worldwide, and AASB/Corporations Act reporting covers the consolidated group. Some ASX-listed foreign entities have no WGEA relevant employer at all.
- Coding: occupations move from ANZSCO to OSCA in the 2027 program; WGEA rounds gaps to one decimal place; a positive gap means men are paid more; WGEA's target range is -5% to +5%.

STATUS SUMMARY (12 Oct 2026). In force: WGE Act (compilation of 4 Apr 2025), GEI Matters Instrument 2023 (amended 2025), Targets Instrument 2025, Standards Instrument 2023, ASX 4th edition. Passed but not in force: Regulatory Reform Omnibus Act 2026 Sch 1 Pt 7 (commences 1 Jan 2027). Draft: ASX 5th edition (2026). Abandoned: ASX 5th edition draft of 2024 (20 Feb 2025). AASB S1 is voluntary and has no gender metric; mandatory AASB S2 is climate only.

I did not open it, and it can be deleted. The shared web-search budget ran out near the end, so these points rest on search summaries, not opened primary text: the WGEA Technical Guide's quartile construction; the exact ASX 4th-edition commencement wording; the 2024 draft's abandonment wording; and the July 2026 draft Rec 2.3(c) text (from Clayton Utz, AICD and CEW). The other-regime clause references in mapsTo (UK, EU, ESRS, BRSR, Japan) are from my own knowledge and should be checked against the other area reports. No files were edited.

instruments.name: Act on the Promotion of Women's Active Engagement in Professional Life (女性の職業生活における活躍の推進に関する法律, Act No. 64 of 2015), Article 20, and its MHLW Ordinance on General Employer Action Plans (平成27年厚生労働省令第162号), Articles 2, 19, 20, 20-2, with the MHLW notices on how to calculate and publish the pay gap and the women-in-management ratio
instruments.status: In force. Pay gap publication has been mandatory for employers with more than 300 regular-basis workers since 8 July 2022. From 1 April 2026, publication of the pay gap AND the women-in-management ratio is mandatory for every employer with 101 or more workers. The Act's expiry date has been extended from 31 March 2026 to 31 March 2036. Nothing has been repealed or struck down.
instruments.effective: The Act came into force on 1 April 2016. MHLW Ordinance No. 104 of 8 July 2022 added the pay gap duty for employers with more than 300 workers. It applies from the business year after the first one ending on or after 8 July 2022, so a March year-end company first published FY ending March 2023 data by about the end of June 2023. Amending Act No. 63 of 11 June 2025 and MHLW Ordinance No. 125 of 23 December 2025 took effect on 1 April 2026. They cover the first business year ending on or after 1 April 2026. A July-June year-end company must publish FY ending June 2026 data by about the end of September 2026. A March year-end company publishes FY ending March 2027 data by about the end of June 2027. MHLW Ordinance No. 18 of 26 February 2026 took effect on 1 October 2026 and contains transitional rules on certification (Art 9-3). The revised MHLW pay gap notice is dated 18 February 2026.
instruments.coverage: Each 一般事業主 (the employing legal entity, not the group) counted by 常時雇用する労働者, which includes part-time and fixed-term staff employed on a continuing basis. Employers with more than 300 workers (Art 20(1)) must publish the pay gap and the women-in-management ratio, plus at least one item from category (1), 'opportunities in working life', and at least one from category (2), 'work-family balance environment', for 4 or more items in total. Employers with 101-300 workers (Art 20(2)) must publish the pay gap and the women-in-management ratio, plus at least one item from either category, for 3 or more items. Employers with 100 or fewer workers are under a duty of effort only (Art 20(3)). Employers with 101 or more workers must also file action plans (Art 8(1)).

measures.name: 男女の賃金の差異 (gender pay gap, published as women's average wage as a % of men's)
measures.definition: Ordinance Art 2(1)(xxiv) and Art 19(1)(i) define it as 'その雇用する労働者の男女の賃金の額の差異'. Art 19(2) requires it for all workers and for each 雇用管理区分 (employment-management category). The MHLW notice requires at least two of those splits: regular and non-regular. Calculation: workers are split by sex and by regular or non-regular. For each group, total wages for the business year are divided by the number of workers (人員数) to give an average annual wage. In principle the number of workers is the average of monthly headcounts over the year. The published value is women's average annual wage divided by men's, × 100, rounded to one decimal. It is published for all workers, for regular workers (正規雇用労働者) and for part-time and fixed-term workers (パート・有期労働者). 'Wages' means everything paid for labour under Labour Standards Act Art 11: salary, allowances and bonuses. Retirement allowances and commuting allowances may be excluded at the employer's discretion, provided the exclusion is stated and applied identically to men and women. An explanatory note and supplementary breakdowns, for example by grade or length of service, are optional.
measures.unit: Percent, women's mean as a percentage of men's (men = 100). This is a ratio, not a gap: gap = 100 − value.
measures.basis: Annual. Mean only, no median. Total pay including bonuses and allowances; retirement and commuting allowances may be excluded. Counted by headcount by default, though part-timers may be converted to FTE using regular workers' scheduled hours, and the conversion must be stated.
measures.population: All workers of the legal entity, plus the mandatory splits into regular (正規雇用労働者: indefinite-term full-time staff, including region-limited and short-hour seishain in MHLW examples) and non-regular (パート・有期: part-time and fixed-term). MHLW examples exclude agency (dispatched) workers. Finer 雇用管理区分 splits, for example career-track and clerical-track, are optional.
measures.period: The most recent completed business year, measured as a flow over 12 months. It is published within about 3 months of the start of the next business year, updated at least annually, with the publication date shown.
mapsTo: JP-FSA-ORD: 労働者の男女の賃金の差異 (official cross-reference in the Form 2 notes; the same figure for the filer and for each consolidated subsidiary)
EU Pay Transparency Directive (EU) 2023/970 Art 9(1)(a) mean gender pay gap — by definition, only after converting with 100 − value, and only if gross annual pay and populations match
UK Equality Act 2010 (Gender Pay Gap Information) Regulations 2017 mean hourly pay gap — looks alike, not comparable (UK uses hourly ordinary pay on a snapshot date, bonuses separately)
ESRS S1-16 gender pay gap — by definition only (ESRS uses gross hourly pay)
Australia WGEA employer gender pay gap (total remuneration, annualised FTE) — by definition; closest when the Japanese employer has used FTE conversion
GRI 405-2 ratio of remuneration of women to men — by definition (same women-to-men direction)
India SEBI BRSR median remuneration by gender — looks alike, not comparable (median, by board/KMP/employee category)

measures.name: 管理職に占める女性労働者の割合 (share of women in management)
measures.definition: Ordinance Art 2(1)(iv) defines it as 'その雇用する管理的地位にある労働者（以下「管理職」という。）に占める女性労働者の割合', and Art 19(1)(ii) makes it mandatory from April 2026. 管理職 means people at 課長級 (section-manager level) or above, excluding officers (役員). 課長級 covers a head of a unit made up of two or more 係, or of a unit with 10 or more members including the head. People with other titles but equivalent duties and responsibilities also count. 課長代理 and 課長補佐 generally do not count. The method is set by the MHLW notice on calculating and publishing the share of women among workers in managerial positions.
measures.basis: Headcount, at a point in time
measures.population: Managers of 課長級 and above in the employing legal entity, excluding officers
measures.period: The most recent business year. The ordinance does not fix a snapshot date (fiscal-year-end is common), so check the MHLW notice and each company's note.

areas.notes:
INTEROPERABLE (officially): Japan has one real chain. The labour laws WAA and CCLA define the figures. The FSA Disclosure Ordinance (Jan 2023 amendment) makes listed filers reproduce those same figures in the securities report, for the filer and for each consolidated subsidiary that publishes them. So for a given legal entity and year, the EDINET figure and the MHLW-database figure should be identical: one calculation rulebook, the MHLW notice of 18 Feb 2026. SSBJ standards are officially aligned with ISSB (comparison and concordance of 31 Mar 2026; IFRS jurisdictional profile of 16 Jul 2026), but they carry no gender metrics. No official mapping exists between any Japanese gender measure and UK, EU, Australian, US or Indian measures; every cross-border link is by definition only.

ONLY LOOKS ALIKE:
(1) Pay gap. Japan publishes women's mean annual pay as a % of men's (e.g. 70.0). The UK, EU, ESRS and WGEA publish a gap, (men − women)/men (e.g. 30.0). Use 100 − value, and only mean-on-mean.
(2) Men's childcare leave rate vs ESRS S1-15 or GRI 401-3. Japan divides men who took any leave in the year (no minimum length) by men whose spouse gave birth in the year. These are different cohorts, so the rate can exceed 100%. There are two permitted variants, one including childcare-purpose leave, and the filer must say which.
(3) Women in management means 課長級 (section manager) and above, excluding officers. This is not ESRS 'top management' or WGEA's manager tiers.
(4) The TSE women-officer ratio may include 執行役員, while the securities report's officer ratio counts statutory officers, including audit and supervisory board members. Neither is the EU or UK 'board' measure.
(5) CGC Principle 2-2 targets are company-defined and not comparable across companies.

TRAPS:
- Hourly vs annual: Japan uses annual pay per head. Part-timers count as 1 head unless the company optionally converts to FTE, and must say so. The 'all workers' figure therefore mixes hours with pay rates. The regular-worker split is the closest to a full-time like-for-like figure.
- Mean vs median: Japan publishes the mean only.
- Base vs total: Japan uses total pay including bonuses, which are large in Japan. Retirement and commuting allowances may be excluded at the employer's discretion. The UK separates ordinary pay and bonus.
- Permanent vs all: 正規雇用労働者 (indefinite-term full-time 'regular' staff) is not 'permanent' in the UK or AU sense. Non-regular means part-time plus fixed-term, and agency workers are excluded. The headcount thresholds (101 or more, 301 or more) count all continuing workers, not regular staff.
- Snapshot: the pay gap is a whole-business-year flow, not a snapshot like the UK's 5 April. The women-in-management ratio is point-in-time, but the ordinance fixes no date. The officer ratio is as of the securities-report filing date, assuming AGM approval.
- Entity: every labour-law figure is per legal employer (単体). A listed holding company's own figure can cover a tiny head-office staff. The securities report lists entity-by-entity figures; a consolidated figure is only encouraged, and foreign subsidiaries are excluded. Do not treat the parent-only figure as the group figure.
- Timing: publication is due within about 3 months of the start of the next business year. 101-300 employers and the women-in-management duty start with the first business year ending on or after 1 Apr 2026. A March year-end company's first figures under the expanded duty are FY2026 data, published by about the end of June 2027. July-June year-end companies are due by about the end of September 2026. Time series for firms with 101-300 workers start there.
- The TSE '2025' target has lapsed as a milestone date. The 2030 30% target remains, without sanction.
- The 2026 CGC abolished supplementary principles, so 'SP 2.4.1' citations are outdated after the July 2027 corporate governance report cycle.

RELATED, NOT CODED AS INSTRUMENTS: the 6th Basic Plan for Gender Equality (Cabinet decision 13 Mar 2026) sets policy targets. Its targets table is a PDF and was not read. The 2024 amendment to the Next Generation Act, effective 1 Apr 2025, reportedly requires employers with 101 or more workers to set numeric targets for men's childcare leave in published action plans; this was not verified against primary text.

METHOD LIMITS: e-Gov statute text was read through the official e-Gov API, plus MHLW, labour bureau, FSA, SSBJ and Gender Equality Bureau HTML pages. The JPX and METI sites returned 403. To respect 'download nothing to disk', I avoided PDFs after one MHLW leaflet (https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/001668255.pdf) was auto-cached unread by the fetch tool at /Users/priyanshu/.claude/projects/-Users-priyanshu-Thoth/48454d65-54cd-4a36-8abe-8225a8e31153/tool-results/webfetch-1791818389933-7cc4sa.pdf. Nothing else was written. nseindia.com and bseindia.com were not fetched. The shared web-search budget ran out before the end.
