- the exact Form 2 note wording, and whether 'publishes voluntarily' triggers the securities-report duty;
- the snapshot rule for the managerial ratio in the Feb 2026 MHLW notice;
- the treatment of seconded workers;
- EDINET XBRL element names;
- where board-gender diversity sits in the 2026 CGC and how the 2026 Code applies by market segment;
- the TSE Appendix 2 text, which was quoted from the TSE outline as returned by search;
- the 2026 Human Capital Visualization Guidelines mapping tables;
- the final outcome of the FSA's 24 Jun 2026 SSBJ designation amendment.

instruments.name: SEBI Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR), updated format: Annexure II to SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-SEC-2/P/CIR/2023/122 (12 Jul 2023), carried as Annexure 16 of the LODR Master Circular (11 Nov 2024, superseded by the Master Circular of 30 Jan 2026)
instruments.status: In force. Mandatory for the top 1000 listed entities under LODR Reg 34(2)(f); voluntary for other listed entities, SME-listed included. Essential Indicators and Section A are mandatory; Leadership Indicators are voluntary. Last format change: SEBI circular of 28 Mar 2025. It reworded Section A Q14-15 to 'assessment or assurance' and added Principle 6 LI 8 (green credits); no gender items changed. I checked the consolidated LODR as amended up to 22 Jan 2026. SEBI lists a further LODR amendment dated 14 Jul 2026 that I did not read.
instruments.effective: BRSR was voluntary for FY2021-22 and mandatory for the top 1000 from FY2022-23, under the 2021 format. Reg 34(2)(f) was substituted w.e.f. 15 Jun 2023. The revised format, which added P5 EI 3(b) gross wages to females, P5 EI 7 POSH complaints and P3 EI 1(c), applies 'for disclosures from FY2023-2024 onwards' (Master Circular, footnote 16). Since 31 Dec 2024 the top-1000 ranking uses average market capitalisation from 1 Jul to 31 Dec. Exchanges prepare the list at 31 Dec and it applies from the following 1 Apr. An entity drops out only after 3 consecutive years outside the threshold (Reg 3(2)-(2B)).
instruments.coverage: Top 1000 listed entities by market capitalisation (see the ranking rule above). The reporting boundary is the entity's choice of standalone or consolidated (Section A Q13), and it must be used consistently across the report. Employees and workers are defined by the Industrial Relations Code 2020 (guidance note).

measures.name: BRSR A-20(a) Employees and workers by gender, permanent and other than permanent
measures.definition: 'Details as at the end of Financial Year: a. Employees and workers (including differently abled)'. Columns: Total (A); Male No. (B), % (B / A); Female No. (C), % (C / A). Rows: Permanent (D), Other than Permanent (E), Total employees (D + E); for workers, Permanent (F), Other than Permanent (G), Total workers (F + G). Guidance definitions: 'Employee' is IR Code 2020 s.2(l). 'Worker' is IR Code s.2(zr), which excludes persons employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity and supervisors drawing over Rs 18,000 a month. 'Permanent' means employed 'for full-time or part-time work, for an indeterminate period'. 'Other than permanent' means fixed-term or task-based staff, who 'could be employed directly by the entity or through third party contractors'. An 'Other' column may be added for persons of another or undisclosed gender.
measures.unit: persons (count) and % of the category total
measures.basis: headcount; no FTE adjustment; full-time and part-time pooled
measures.population: employees and workers reported separately, each split permanent / other than permanent; 'other than permanent' includes contract labour supplied by contractors
measures.period: as at the end of the financial year (normally 31 March); reasons to be given if the number changed significantly during the year
mapsTo: GRI 2-7 a-b (headcount by gender; permanent vs temporary): matches by definition, since BRSR's permanent / other-than-permanent wording copies GRI's. BRSR's contractor-supplied workers belong in GRI 2-8 (workers who are not employees), not 2-7.
ESRS S1-6 para 50(a)-(b): matches by definition for directly employed staff; contractor-supplied staff fall under ESRS S1-7 (non-employees)
IN-CAR-2025 Extract of Board Report headcount (Female/Male/Transgender): matches by definition, but the population is undefined and the boundary is the standalone company
SASB industry gender-representation metrics (e.g. TC-SI-330a.3): looks alike only (they are by job level)

measures.name: BRSR A-20(b) Differently abled employees and workers by gender
measures.definition: 'b. Differently abled Employees and workers': the same Total / Male / Female table for Permanent (D), Other than Permanent (E), Total differently abled employees (D + E), Permanent (F), Other than permanent (G), Total differently abled workers (F + G). Persons are identified under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016.
measures.population: differently abled employees and workers, permanent / other than permanent
measures.period: as at the end of the financial year
mapsTo: ESRS S1-12 (percentage of employees with disabilities; breakdown by gender optional): matches by definition, partially
GRI 405-1 b (other diversity indicators): looks alike only

measures.name: BRSR A-21 Women on the Board of Directors
measures.definition: 'Participation/Inclusion/Representation of women': Board of Directors, Total (A), 'No. and percentage of Females' No. (B), % (B / A). Board as defined in Companies Act s.2(10).
measures.basis: headcount of directors (executive and non-executive together)
measures.period: date not specified in the format or the guidance; in practice usually at the end of the financial year
mapsTo: GRI 405-1 a(i): matches by definition
ESRS 2 GOV-1 para 21(d): same concept, but ESRS computes board gender diversity as an average ratio of female to male members, not a share
IN-LODR-17 and IN-CA-149: these are compliance floors (at least one woman), not counts

EU Women on Boards Directive 2022/2381; UK Listing Rules board diversity targets; ASX Recommendation 1.5; Japan securities report female officer ratio: match by definition, but check whether each counts executive and non-executive directors the same way

measures.name: BRSR A-21 Women among Key Management Personnel
measures.definition: The same table row for 'Key Management Personnel'. KMP as defined in Companies Act s.2(51): CEO, managing director or manager; company secretary; whole-time director; CFO; and other prescribed officers.
measures.population: statutory KMP, usually 3 to 6 people, who may overlap with the board (MD and WTD)
measures.period: not specified (usually the end of the financial year)
mapsTo: ESRS S1-9 para 66(a) gender distribution at top management: looks alike only (a much wider population)
Japan ratio of women in managerial positions; WGEA manager categories: looks alike only
UK Listing Rules senior board positions / executive management: looks alike only

measures.name: BRSR A-22 Turnover rate of permanent employees and permanent workers by gender
measures.definition: 'Turnover rate for permanent employees and workers (Disclose trends for the past 3 years)': Male, Female and Total for Permanent Employees and Permanent Workers, for the current FY, the previous FY and the year before that. Guidance formula: '(No. of persons who have left the employment of the entity in the FY *100) / Average no. of persons employed in the category', where the average is (start-of-FY + end-of-FY)/2. Leavers include those leaving 'voluntarily or due to dismissal, termination, retirement or death in service'.
measures.basis: headcount; average of opening and closing headcount
measures.population: permanent employees and permanent workers only
mapsTo: GRI 401-1 b (rate of employee turnover by gender): matches by definition (same leaver scope as GRI 401 guidance; GRI does not fix the denominator)
ESRS S1-6 para 50(c) (number of leavers and turnover rate; no gender split required): matches partially

measures.name: BRSR P3 EI-1(a),(b) Well-being benefit coverage by gender
measures.definition: 'Details of measures for the well-being of employees' and '... of workers': for Permanent and Other than Permanent, Male / Female / Total. Total (A), then Number and % covered by Health insurance (B), Accident insurance (C), Maternity benefits (D), Paternity Benefits (E) and Day Care facilities (F).
measures.population: employees and workers, permanent and other than permanent
mapsTo: GRI 401-2 (benefits for full-time employees; no gender split): looks alike only
ESRS S1-11 social protection; ESRS S1-15 entitlement to family-related leave: looks alike only
Code on Social Security 2020 maternity and creche entitlements: the legal basis of the maternity and day-care items

measures.name: BRSR P3 EI-5 Return to work and retention after parental leave, by gender
measures.definition: 'Return to work and Retention rates of permanent employees and workers that took parental leave': Male / Female / Total, for permanent employees and permanent workers. Guidance: parental leave 'refers to maternity and paternity leave'. Return to work rate = employees who did return after parental leave in the period x 100 / employees due to return in the period. Retention rate = 'Total number of employees retained 12 months after returning to work following a period of parental leave * 100' / employees returning from parental leave in the prior reporting period.
measures.period: reporting period; retention looks back to returns in the prior period
mapsTo: GRI 401-3 d-e: matches by definition (identical formulas)
ESRS S1-15 para 93 (entitlement to and take-up of family-related leave by gender): looks alike only
Japan childcare-leave uptake rates: looks alike only

measures.name: BRSR P3 EI-7 Union or association membership by gender
measures.definition: 'Membership of employees and worker in association(s) or Unions recognised by the listed entity': Total permanent employees or workers in the category (A), number who are members (B), % (B / A), with Male and Female rows, for the current and previous FY.
mapsTo: GRI 2-30 and ESRS S1-8 (collective bargaining coverage; no gender split): looks alike only (membership is not coverage)

measures.name: BRSR P3 EI-8 Training by gender
measures.definition: 'Details of training given to employees and workers': for Employees and Workers, Male / Female / Total. Total (A); 'On Health and safety measures' No. (B), % (B / A); 'On Skill upgradation' No. (C), % (C / A); current and previous FY.
measures.population: employees and workers (not split by permanence)
mapsTo: GRI 404-1 and ESRS S1-13 para 83(b) (average training hours by gender): looks alike only

measures.name: BRSR P3 EI-9 Performance and career development reviews by gender
measures.definition: 'Details of performance and career development reviews of employees and worker': Total (A), No. (B), % (B / A), Male / Female / Total, current and previous FY. Guidance: a review 'based on criteria known to the employee / worker and his or her superior'.
mapsTo: GRI 404-3: matches by definition
ESRS S1-13 para 83(a): matches by definition

measures.name: BRSR P5 EI-2 Minimum-wage status by gender
measures.definition: 'Details of minimum wages paid to employees and workers': for Employees and Workers, Permanent and Other than Permanent, Male and Female. Total (A); 'Equal to Minimum Wage' No. (B), % (B / A); 'More than Minimum Wage' No. (C), % (C / A); current and previous FY.
measures.basis: headcount by wage band relative to the statutory minimum
measures.population: employees and workers, permanent and other than permanent
mapsTo: GRI 202-1 (entry-level wage by gender vs local minimum wage): looks alike only
ESRS S1-10 adequate wages: looks alike only
Code on Wages 2019 minimum wage provisions: the legal reference

measures.name: BRSR P5 EI-3(a) Median remuneration by gender and category
measures.definition: 'Details of remuneration/salary/wages a. Median remuneration / wages': for Board of Directors (BoD), Key Managerial Personnel, Employees other than BoD and KMP, and Workers, the Male Number and 'Median remuneration/ salary/ wages of respective category', and the same for Female. The guidance cites three definitions without choosing between them. Remuneration (Companies Act s.2(78), includes perquisites). Salary (Income-tax Act: wages, pension, gratuity, fees, commissions, perquisites, advance of salary). Wages (Code on Wages s.2(y)).
measures.basis: annual; median; pay concept is mixed (total remuneration for BoD and KMP, wages or salary for others); not hourly, not FTE
measures.population: four categories; whether workers or employees include other-than-permanent staff is not specified; BoD median includes non-executive sitting fees and commission
mapsTo: GRI 405-2 (ratio of basic salary and remuneration of women to men by employee category and significant location): looks alike only; a female/male median ratio can be derived, but basic salary is not separated
ESRS S1-16 para 97(a) (mean gross hourly gender pay gap): looks alike only
UK Gender Pay Gap Regulations 2017 median hourly gap; EU Directive 2023/970 Art 9 median gap: looks alike only (annual vs hourly; categories differ)
Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules 2014 r.5(1) median remuneration of employees (no gender split): matches by definition, partially

measures.name: BRSR P5 EI-3(b) Gross wages paid to females as % of total wages
measures.definition: 'b. Gross wages paid to females as % of total wages paid by the entity', for the current and previous FY. The 2021 guidance note has no entry for it. The ISF standards (IN-ISF-BRSRCORE) govern its computation.
measures.basis: annual gross wages over the FY; total cash pay (ISF: salaries, bonuses and other compensation; excludes retirement benefits and ESOPs); not hourly, not FTE, not a pay gap
measures.population: wages 'paid by the entity', i.e. its own payroll. Wages of contractor-supplied workers are often outside it, while those workers sit in A-20 headcount.
mapsTo: No direct counterpart in GRI, ESRS or ISSB

With A-20 headcount it gives an implied mean annual female/male pay ratio, which approximates Japan's women-to-men wage difference (mean annual) and WGEA's average total remuneration gap (annualised FTE): matches by definition, approximately
ESRS S1-16 gender pay gap: looks alike only
IN-BRSR-CORE Attribute 6: the same datapoint, assessed or assured

measures.name: BRSR P5 EI-6 Complaints on sexual harassment and discrimination
measures.definition: 'Number of Complaints on the following made by employees and workers': Sexual Harassment; Discrimination at workplace (also child labour, forced labour, wages, other human rights). For each: Filed during the year, Pending resolution at the end of year, Remarks; current and previous FY.
measures.basis: complaints filed in the FY; pending at FY end
mapsTo: GRI 406-1 (incidents of discrimination): matches by definition, partially
ESRS S1-17 para 103(a) (incidents of discrimination including harassment): matches by definition, partially

measures.name: BRSR P5 EI-7 Complaints under the POSH Act
measures.definition: 'Complaints filed under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013'. Rows: Total Complaints reported under POSH; 'Complaints on POSH as a % of female employees / workers'; 'Complaints on POSH upheld'. Current and previous FY.
measures.unit: count; % of female employees and workers; count upheld
measures.basis: complaints in the FY divided by female headcount (the ISF standards clarify the denominator; I could not retrieve that text)
mapsTo: IN-CAR-2025 r.8(5)(x)(a) complaints received in the year: matches by definition (same Act, same FY)
IN-POSH Rule 14(a)-(b): matches by definition, but on a calendar year, not the FY
ESRS S1-17: looks alike only

instruments.publicAccess: Public and free. Published as part of the annual report (Reg 34(2)(f)) on the company website and the stock exchanges. Also filed as XBRL with the exchanges. Your own Nifty 50 pipeline reads XBRL tags such as TotalWagesPaid and GrossWagesPaidToFemale, i.e. rupee amounts, not only the %. I did not fetch exchange sites.
interop: IN-BRSR-GN para 1 'Inter-operability of reporting framework' (cross-referencing to GRI, SASB, TCFD, Integrated Reporting)
LODR Master Circular Ch. IV-B para 1.5 (same cross-reference permission)
IN-BRSR-CORE 'Cross-reference to the BRSR' column
Guidance note: 'prepared using references from' the NGRBC, the GRI Standards and Indian laws (MCA National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct 2019 = the nine principles)
instruments.quote: Gross wages paid to females as % of total wages paid by the entity

instruments.name: BRSR Core (Annexure I to SEBI circular of 12 Jul 2023; Annexure 17A of the LODR Master Circular; revised by circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 of 28 Mar 2025)
instruments.status: In force. A subset of BRSR KPIs, so all top-1000 entities disclose them. Third-party 'assessment' (under the ISF standards) or 'assurance' is mandatory along a glide path. Value-chain BRSR Core disclosures are voluntary.
instruments.effective: Assessment or assurance applies to: top 150 for FY2023-24; top 250 for FY2024-25; top 500 for FY2025-26; top 1000 for FY2026-27 (the year in progress on 12 Oct 2026). Before 28 Mar 2025 only reasonable assurance was allowed; the assessment option applies from that circular. Value chain (partners with 2% or more of purchases or sales; may be limited to 75% coverage) is voluntary for the top 250 from FY2025-26, with voluntary assessment or assurance from FY2026-27.
instruments.coverage: Top 1000 listed entities, phased as above; same boundary choice as BRSR

measures.name: BRSR Core Attribute 6 'Enabling Gender Diversity in Business': gross wages paid to females
measures.definition: Parameter: 'Gross wages paid to females as % of wages paid'. Measurement: 'In % terms'. Data & assessment or assurance approach: 'Employee Master / Register'. Cross-reference: Principle 5, Question 3(b) of Essential Indicators.
measures.basis: annual gross wages; total pay as defined by the ISF standards; not hourly
mapsTo: IN-BRSR P5 EI-3(b): the same datapoint (official cross-reference in the BRSR Core format)
No GRI, ESRS or ISSB counterpart

measures.name: BRSR Core Attribute 6: complaints on POSH
measures.definition: Parameter: 'Complaints on POSH'. Measurements: 'Total Complaints on Sexual Harassment (POSH) reported'; 'Complaints on POSH as a % of female employees / workers'; 'Complaints on POSH upheld'. Cross-reference: Principle 5, Question 7 of Essential Indicators.
measures.basis: FY complaint counts over female headcount
mapsTo: IN-BRSR P5 EI-7: the same datapoint (official cross-reference)
IN-CAR-2025 r.8(5)(x): matches by definition

instruments.publicAccess: Public: the BRSR section of the annual report, naming the assessment or assurance provider and the type obtained (Section A Q14-15); XBRL on the exchanges
interop: Official 'Cross-reference to the BRSR' column in the BRSR Core format
Master Circular para 2.1: PPP-adjusted revenue intensity ratios 'for better global comparability' (environmental KPIs only, not gender)
instruments.quote: few new KPIs have been identified for assessment or assurance such as job creation in small towns, open-ness of business, gross wages paid to women etc.

instruments.name: Guidance Note for BRSR (Annexure II to SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD-2/P/CIR/2021/562 of 10 May 2021; now Annexure 17 of the LODR Master Circular, renumbered to the 2023 format)
instruments.status: In force as SEBI's interpretive guidance. The Master Circular version is renumbered (Q20-22), but it has no guidance for the 2023 additions (P5 EI 3(b), P5 EI 7); the ISF standards fill that gap for BRSR Core.
instruments.effective: From FY2021-22 (with BRSR)
instruments.coverage: Entities preparing BRSR
instruments.publicAccess: Public (SEBI website, inside the circular and the Master Circular)
interop: Para 1 'Inter-operability of reporting framework': entities may cross-reference GRI, SASB, TCFD or Integrated Reporting disclosures, giving the page number. This is a cross-reference permission, not a datapoint mapping table.

Closing note: guidance 'prepared using references from' the NGRBC, the GRI sustainability reporting standards and Indian laws. The parental-leave, turnover-leaver, permanent/temporary and performance-review definitions are taken from GRI.
Para 7: an 'Other' gender column may be added
Para 2: the reporting boundary must be consistent across the report
instruments.quote: can cross-reference the disclosures made under such framework to the disclosures sought under the BRSR

instruments.name: Industry Standards on Reporting of BRSR Core (Industry Standards Forum: ASSOCHAM, CII, FICCI, under the aegis of the stock exchanges), mandated by SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/177 of 20 Dec 2024
instruments.status: In force; listed entities 'shall follow' them. Since 28 Mar 2025 they are also the basis of third-party 'assessment'. I could not retrieve the standards text: it is hosted on the NSE/BSE and industry-association sites, and I did not fetch those. The content below comes from a secondary summary (ESG360, 26 Dec 2024).
instruments.effective: FY2024-25 onwards
instruments.coverage: All entities disclosing BRSR Core

measures.name: ISF computation rule for gross wages paid to females (Attribute 6)
measures.definition: Per the secondary summary: wages include salaries, bonuses and other compensation, excluding retirement benefits and ESOPs. A bonus accrued but not paid is apportioned proportionately between genders. For the wage-based inclusive-development KPI, total wages count staff whether permanent or contractual, excluding retirement benefits, ESOPs and staff welfare. For POSH, the standards are said to clarify the % denominator and define 'complaints on POSH upheld' (wording not verified).
measures.basis: annual; total cash compensation excluding retirement benefits and ESOP
measures.population: entity payroll; contractual staff included per the summary (verify against the standard)
mapsTo: IN-BRSR P5 EI-3(b) and IN-BRSR-CORE Attribute 6: defines them

instruments.publicAccess: Public: on the ASSOCHAM, CII, FICCI and exchange websites
interop: Operationalises IN-BRSR-CORE
instruments.quote: The listed entities shall follow the above industry standards to ensure compliance with SEBI requirements on disclosure of BRSR Core.

instruments.name: SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015, Regulation 17(1)(a): woman director and independent woman director
instruments.status: In force. Text checked in the consolidated LODR as amended up to 22 Jan 2026; the 14 Jul 2026 amendment was not checked.
instruments.effective: Woman director: since LODR commenced in 2015, earlier under the listing agreement. Independent woman director: top 500 by 1 Apr 2019 and top 1000 by 1 Apr 2020 (footnotes 134-136). Reworded w.e.f. 31 Dec 2024 to 'top 1000 listed entities', now ranked by average market capitalisation (Reg 3(2)).
instruments.coverage: Every listed entity with listed specified securities, except those exempt under Reg 15(2): paid-up equity up to Rs 10 crore and net worth up to Rs 25 crore, and SME-exchange listings. Independent woman director: top 1000.

measures.name: At least one woman director
measures.definition: 'board of directors shall have an optimum combination of executive and non-executive directors with at least one woman director'
mapsTo: IN-CA-149: the same floor for listed companies
IN-BRSR A-21: gives the actual count
EU Directive 2022/2381; UK Listing Rules targets; ASX Rec 1.5: looks alike only (the Indian rule is a floor of one, not a share)

measures.name: At least one independent woman director (top 1000)
measures.definition: 'Provided that the Board of directors of the top 1000 listed entities shall have at least one independent woman director'
mapsTo: IN-BRSR A-21 (does not split independent directors): partial

instruments.publicAccess: Public: board composition is disclosed in the annual report's corporate governance report (Schedule V) and in the quarterly corporate governance compliance reports filed with exchanges (Reg 27(2)). I did not verify that those formats carry an explicit gender field; BRSR A-21 does.
interop: Shares its threshold with IN-BRSR (top 1000, Reg 3(2) ranking)
instruments.quote: board of directors shall have an optimum combination of executive and non-executive directors with at least one woman director

instruments.name: Companies Act 2013 s.149(1) second proviso, with Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014, Rule 3
instruments.status: In force (Rule 3 text reproduced as valid on 12 Oct 2026)
instruments.effective: s.149 from 1 Apr 2014. New companies must comply within 6 months of incorporation. A vacancy must be filled 'at the earliest but not later than immediate next Board meeting or three months from the date of such vacancy whichever is later'.
instruments.coverage: Every listed company, and every other public company with paid-up share capital of Rs 100 crore or more or turnover of Rs 300 crore or more, measured at the last date of the latest audited financial statements. Private companies are not covered.

measures.name: At least one woman director (prescribed classes)
measures.definition: s.149(1): 'such class or classes of companies as may be prescribed, shall have at least one woman director'. Rule 3: 'The following class of companies shall appoint at least one woman director'.
mapsTo: IN-LODR-17: the same floor
IN-BRSR A-21: gives the count

instruments.publicAccess: Director lists are public on MCA21 company master data and in annual returns (MGT-7; viewing documents costs a fee). I did not verify a gender field. Listed companies' annual reports are free.
interop: Companies Act s.2(10) Board and s.2(51) KMP definitions are the ones BRSR A-21 uses
instruments.quote: The following class of companies shall appoint at least one woman director

instruments.name: Companies (Accounts) Rules 2014, rule 8(5)(x) and new (xiii), with the e-form 'Extract of Board Report', as amended by the Companies (Accounts) Second Amendment Rules 2025 (G.S.R. 357(E), 30 May 2025)
instruments.status: In force
instruments.effective: 14 Jul 2025. Rule 8(5)(x) previously required only a statement on constituting the Internal Complaints Committee. The new rule 12(1C) requires the Extract of Board Report e-form to be filed with AOC-4 / AOC-4 CFS.
instruments.coverage: Every company preparing a board's report under s.134, listed or unlisted, public or private. The board's report is prepared on the standalone financial statements (rule 8(1)).

measures.name: Sexual harassment complaints received in the year
measures.definition: Rule 8(5)(x), after the ICC-constitution statement, 'along with the following details': '(a) number of complaints of sexual harassment received in the year'
mapsTo: IN-BRSR P5 EI-7 'Total complaints reported': matches by definition
IN-POSH Rule 14(a): matches by definition, but on a calendar year

measures.name: Sexual harassment complaints disposed off
measures.definition: '(b) number of complaints disposed off during the year'
mapsTo: IN-POSH Rule 14(b) and s.22 'disposal': matches by definition
IN-BRSR P5 EI-7 'upheld': looks alike only (disposed is not the same as upheld)

measures.name: Cases pending more than ninety days
measures.definition: '(c) number of cases pending for more than ninety days'
mapsTo: IN-POSH Rule 14(c): matches by definition
IN-BRSR P5 EI-6 'pending resolution at the end of year': looks alike only (it includes all pending, not only those over 90 days)

measures.name: Statement of compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act 1961
measures.definition: New clause (xiii): a statement by the company with respect to compliance with the provisions relating to the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 (e-form: 'Statement that company has complied with Maternity Benefit Act').
mapsTo: IN-BRSR P3 EI-1 maternity benefit coverage: looks alike only

measures.name: Number of employees by gender at year end (Extract of Board Report)
measures.definition: E-form 'Extract of Board Report', item (j): 'Number of employees as on the closure of financial year': Female, Male, Transgender. The e-form is part of the notified Annexure; I did not check whether the field is starred mandatory. 'Employee' is not defined in the form.
measures.population: employees of the company (standalone); whether contract labour is included is undefined
measures.period: as on the closure of the financial year
mapsTo: IN-BRSR A-20(a): matches by definition, but the population and boundary differ, and it adds a Transgender category that BRSR lacks
GRI 2-7; ESRS S1-6: match by definition

instruments.publicAccess: The board's report is in the annual report (free for listed companies). Filed e-forms can be viewed on MCA21 public documents for a fee; I found no open dataset.
interop: Overlaps with IN-BRSR P5 EI-7 and IN-POSH s.22 / Rule 14
instruments.quote: (a) number of complaints of sexual harassment received in the year;

instruments.name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act 2013, ss.21-22, and the 2013 Rules, rule 14 (annual report)
instruments.status: In force; not subsumed by the labour codes
instruments.effective: 9 Dec 2013 (Act and Rules)
instruments.coverage: Every employer. An Internal Committee is required where there are 10 or more employees (s.4); otherwise the Local Committee applies. 'Employee' (s.2(f)) is broad: regular, temporary, ad hoc, daily-wage, staff engaged through an agent or contractor, trainees and interns.

measures.name: Cases filed and their disposal (employer's annual report)
measures.definition: s.22: the employer shall include in its report the number of cases filed, if any, and their disposal under this Act in the annual report of the organisation; where no annual report is required, it intimates the numbers to the District Officer
mapsTo: IN-CAR-2025 r.8(5)(x): implements it for companies
IN-BRSR P5 EI-7: matches by definition

measures.name: Internal or Local Committee annual report contents
measures.definition: Rule 14: (a) number of complaints of sexual harassment received in the year; (b) number of complaints disposed off during the year; (c) number of cases pending for more than ninety days; (d) number of workshops or awareness programmes against sexual harassment carried out; (e) nature of action taken by the employer or District Officer
measures.period: calendar year (January to December), not the April-March FY
mapsTo: IN-CAR-2025 (a)-(c): copies items (a)-(c), but on the FY

instruments.publicAccess: The Internal Committee report goes to the employer and the District Officer and is not public. The s.22 numbers are public only through a public annual report. SHe-Box (Ministry of Women and Child Development) does not publish company data.
interop: Feeds IN-CAR-2025 and IN-BRSR P5 EI-7

instruments.name: Code on Wages 2019 (Act 29 of 2019): s.3 non-discrimination on the ground of gender; s.2(y) definition of wages
instruments.status: Enacted 8 Aug 2019. All four labour codes were brought into force on 21 Nov 2025. areas.notes:
INTEROPERABLE (same thing, by definition; there is no official BRSR-to-ESRS or BRSR-to-ISSB mapping). (1) BRSR A-20 headcount by gender and permanence matches GRI 2-7 and ESRS S1-6, for directly employed staff only. (2) BRSR A-21 women on the board matches GRI 405-1a. ESRS GOV-1 21(d) expresses the same thing as a female-to-male ratio instead of a share. (3) BRSR A-22 turnover by gender matches GRI 401-1b (same leaver scope). (4) BRSR P3 EI-5 parental leave return and retention matches GRI 401-3; the formulas are identical. (5) BRSR P3 EI-9 performance reviews matches GRI 404-3 and ESRS S1-13 83(a). (6) Complaint counts in BRSR P5 EI-6/7, the Companies (Accounts) Rules 8(5)(x) and POSH Rule 14 are the same counts, except that POSH runs on a calendar year. Most BRSR social definitions are taken from GRI; the guidance note says so.

ONLY LOOKS ALIKE. (1) BRSR P5 EI-3(a) gives annual medians per gender per category (BoD, KMP, other employees, workers), with a mixed pay concept. GRI 405-2 is a basic-salary and remuneration ratio. ESRS S1-16, the UK regulations and the EU Pay Transparency Directive are hourly gaps. (2) BRSR P3 EI-8 counts people trained; GRI 404-1 and ESRS S1-13 count training hours. (3) BRSR P5 EI-2 minimum-wage bands are not GRI 202-1. (4) BRSR P3 EI-7 counts union membership; GRI 2-30 and ESRS S1-8 count collective bargaining coverage. (5) Women in KMP is not ESRS 'top management' and not Japan's or WGEA's 'managers'. BRSR has no women-in-management measure at all.

NO COUNTERPART. P5 EI-3(b), female share of gross wages, which BRSR Core assesses or assures, has no counterpart in GRI, ESRS or ISSB. IFRS S1 and S2 have no gender metrics. The ISSB only touches gender through some SASB industry metrics on gender representation by job level (e.g. TC-SI-330a.3, cited from memory), and these only partly match A-20/A-21. Combining 3(b) with headcount gives an implied mean annual pay ratio, R = [w/(1-w)] x [M/F]. This roughly matches Japan's mean-annual wage difference and WGEA's average total-remuneration gap; it is not an ESRS or UK gap.

OFFICIAL INTEROPERABILITY DOCUMENTS. These are cross-reference permissions, not datapoint maps:
- the BRSR Guidance Note's 'Inter-operability of reporting framework' paragraph (GRI, SASB, TCFD, IR)
- the LODR Master Circular Ch. IV-B para 1.5
- the BRSR Core 'Cross-reference to the BRSR' column
- the NGRBC 2019, which supplies the nine principles

A GRI-published BRSR linkage document probably exists, but I did not retrieve it, so treat it as unverified. Onward chain: the GRI-ESRS interoperability index and the ESRS-ISSB interoperability guidance (not fetched; other lanes).

TRAPS.
- Hourly vs annual: every Indian pay figure is an annual FY amount. Nothing is hourly or FTE-adjusted, and BRSR 'permanent' pools full-time and part-time staff.
- Mean vs median: 3(a) is a median; 3(b) is a wage-bill share, which becomes a mean only if you divide by headcount.
- Base vs total: 3(b) is total cash pay (per the ISF: bonuses in; retirement benefits and ESOPs out). For 3(a) the guidance offers the Companies Act remuneration, the Income-tax salary or Code on Wages wages (basic + DA, with a 50% add-back) without choosing.
- Permanent vs all staff: 'other than permanent' includes contractor-supplied labour, which GRI 2-8 and ESRS S1-7 treat as non-employees. Wages 'paid by the entity' often exclude that labour while headcount includes it. Your own Nifty 50 test saw L&T at 3.6x before switching to permanent headcount (/Users/priyanshu/Thoth/knowledge/research/nifty50-gender-payroll-footprint.md). Turnover and parental-leave rates are permanent staff only. Employees and workers follow the IR Code split; add them together for total staff.
- Snapshot date: A-20 headcount and the Companies Act extract are at FY end (usually 31 March). A-21 has no stated date. Pay and complaints cover April to March. POSH committee reports are January to December.
- Entity vs group: the BRSR boundary is the company's choice. KPMG found 61 standalone, 32 consolidated and 1 both among 94 Nifty 100 filers for FY2024-25; your FY2025-26 Nifty 50 test found 34 standalone and 16 consolidated. The board's report and its headcount are standalone, while market cap is group-wide.
- Other: the 2021 guidance numbered these questions Q18-20, which are now Q20-22. 3(b) and EI-7 exist only from FY2023-24 reports. KMP overlaps the board. The BoD median includes non-executive fees. BRSR has an optional 'Other' gender column, while the MCA form has 'Transgender'. Assurance levels are mixed (assessment vs reasonable assurance; the top 1000 are only covered from FY2026-27). Rule 8(5)(xiii) cites the Maternity Benefit Act 1961, which the Code on Social Security repeals on commencement.

- The shared web-search budget ran out mid-task.
- India Code, MCA, labour.gov.in, PIB and e-Gazette returned 403 or connection errors. As a result, the Companies Act s.149 text, POSH s.22, the Code on Wages s.3, the 21 Nov 2025 labour-code commencement and the ERA and BRR measures are partly from memory.
- The ISF standards text was not retrieved; that content is from a secondary summary.
- Rule 3 and the G.S.R. 357(E) gazette scan were read from ca2013.com copies.
- SEBI's 14 Jul 2026 LODR amendment and the Annexure numbering in the 30 Jan 2026 Master Circular were not checked.
- NSE and BSE were not fetched.

instruments.name: SEC Regulation S-K Item 101(c)(2)(ii): human capital resources
instruments.status: In force. Under review: on 13 Jan 2026 SEC Chair Atkins launched a wholesale review of Regulation S-K (File CLL-15; comments closed 13 Apr 2026). Some commenters, including Business Roundtable, asked for the human capital requirement to be eliminated; others asked for standardised metrics. No proposal to amend Item 101(c)(2)(ii) was found in sources up to mid-2026. A separate proposal of 19 May 2026 (Release 33-11419, comments to 20 Jul 2026) would give non-accelerated filers a shorter Item 101 business description. Two earlier pushes for workforce metrics were never adopted: the 2021-24 human capital rulemaking agenda item and the Investor Advisory Committee recommendation of 21 Sep 2023.
instruments.effective: Adopted 26 Aug 2020 (Release 33-10825, Modernization of Regulation S-K Items 101, 103 and 105; 85 FR 63726, 8 Oct 2020); effective 9 Nov 2020.
instruments.coverage: Domestic SEC registrants filing Form 10-K and registration statements that call for Item 101 (S-1, S-4, Form 10). Smaller reporting companies are covered under scaled Item 101(h). Foreign private issuers filing Form 20-F are not covered; they give employee numbers under 20-F Item 6.D instead. The item is limited by materiality: 'to the extent material to an understanding of, the registrant's business taken as a whole'.

measures.name: Number of persons employed by the registrant
measures.definition: 'A description of the registrant's human capital resources, including the number of persons employed by the registrant'. The rule does not define the term: it gives no instruction on full-time versus part-time, FTE, contractors, geography or date.
measures.basis: Headcount as the registrant chooses: most give total headcount, some full-time only, some FTE. Not broken down by gender.
measures.population: Registrant and its consolidated subsidiaries, worldwide unless the filer says otherwise
mapsTo: US-EEO1-C1 total employees (looks alike only: EEO-1 counts US payroll employees in a Q4 pay period)
Form 20-F Item 6.D number of employees (by definition)
Workforce denominators in UK GPG Regs 2017, EU Directive 2023/970, Australia WGEA and India BRSR (by definition only; the populations differ)

measures.name: Human capital measures or objectives (any gender or diversity metric)
measures.definition: 'any human capital measures or objectives that the registrant focuses on in managing the business (such as, depending on the nature of the registrant's business and workforce, measures or objectives that address the development, attraction and retention of personnel)'. No gender or diversity metric is named or required. Any figure for % women, women in management or pay equity is the registrant's own choice and definition.
measures.basis: Registrant-defined. Common choices: % women in the global workforce, % women in leadership, an 'adjusted' pay equity ratio. Unadjusted gaps are rare.
measures.population: Registrant-defined (global, US-only, or 'leadership' as each company defines it)
mapsTo: No official mapping. Voluntary content often reuses US-EEO1-C1 categories, GRI 405-1/405-2 or SASB '330a' diversity metrics (by definition)

instruments.publicAccess: Public: Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR, free.
interop: No official equivalence with any non-US regime.
The 2020 adopting release deliberately declined to mandate diversity metrics. Commissioners Lee and Crenshaw dissented partly on that ground.
instruments.quote: any human capital measures or objectives that the registrant focuses on in managing the business

instruments.name: SEC Regulation S-K Item 407(c)(2)(vi): consideration of diversity for director nominees (2009 Proxy Disclosure Enhancements), with staff C&DIs 116.11 (Item 401) and 133.13 (Item 407)
instruments.status: In force. Challenged: a petition for rulemaking from America First Legal Foundation dated 12 Jun 2026 (SEC petition 4-904) asks the SEC to (a) rescind the diversity language, (b) replace it with a certification that sex, race and similar characteristics were not considered and that no target or metric was applied, and (c) rescind C&DIs 116.11 and 133.13. No SEC action on the petition was found. C&DI 116.11 still appeared on the SEC's Regulation S-K C&DI page in Oct 2026. The item also falls within the Jan 2026 Regulation S-K review.
instruments.effective: Release 33-9089 adopted 16 Dec 2009, effective 28 Feb 2010. C&DIs 116.11 and 133.13 issued 6 Feb 2019.
instruments.coverage: Registrants that file proxy or information statements for director elections (Schedule 14A/14C) or include Part III in Form 10-K. In practice domestic issuers; foreign private issuers on Form 20-F are not subject.

measures.name: Whether and how diversity is considered in identifying director nominees
measures.definition: 'whether, and if so how, the nominating committee (or the board) considers diversity in identifying nominees for director'. 'Diversity' is not defined, and companies may define it as they choose. Gender is not required.
mapsTo: US-WA-23B.08.120 board diversity discussion and analysis (by definition, similar narrative)
US-IL-805-8.12 description of the nominee process (by definition)
UK FCA UKLR board diversity comply-or-explain statement (looks alike: the UK adds numeric targets and a standard table)
EU Directive 2022/2381 board gender reporting (looks alike)

measures.name: Diversity policy: implementation and effectiveness
measures.definition: 'If the nominating committee (or the board) has a policy with regard to the consideration of diversity in identifying director nominees, describe how this policy is implemented, as well as how the nominating committee (or the board) assesses the effectiveness of its policy'.
mapsTo: ASX Corporate Governance Principles Rec. 1.5 diversity policy (looks alike)
Japan Corporate Governance Code board diversity principles (looks alike)

measures.name: Self-identified diversity characteristics of directors and nominees (staff C&DI 116.11/133.13)
measures.definition: Staff expectation, not a rule. Where the board considered a nominee's self-identified diversity characteristics (for example gender) and the nominee consented to disclosure, the Item 401 discussion should identify those characteristics and say how they were considered. No count or percentage is required.
measures.unit: Per-director characteristic or narrative. Many companies voluntarily give a count or % of women directors.
measures.basis: Headcount of directors, where a figure is given
mapsTo: US-NASDAQ-5605f-5606 Board Diversity Matrix 'Female' count (by definition; vacated)
% women on board under UK UKLR, the EU Women on Boards Directive, ASX and India BRSR/Companies Act (by definition only)

instruments.publicAccess: Public: proxy statements (DEF 14A) and Form 10-K on EDGAR.
interop: No official foreign equivalence.
Nasdaq Rule 5606 (now vacated) was built to add standard counts on top of Item 407.

instruments.name: Nasdaq Listing Rules 5605(f) (Diverse Board Representation), 5606 (Board Diversity Disclosure, the Board Diversity Matrix) and IM-5900-9 (board recruiting service)
instruments.jurisdiction: United States (Nasdaq Stock Market; SEC-approved SRO rule)
instruments.status: Vacated and deleted. On 11 Dec 2024 the en banc Fifth Circuit vacated the SEC order approving the rules (Alliance for Fair Board Recruitment v. SEC, No. 21-60626, 9-8), holding that the SEC acted beyond its Exchange Act authority. Nasdaq did not seek review. It filed SR-NASDAQ-2025-007 (21 Jan 2025) to delete the rules, operative on filing and effective 4 Feb 2025 (SEC notice reported as Release 34-102281). No obligation remains.
instruments.effective: SEC approval 6 Aug 2021 (Release 34-92590). The first matrix was due by the later of 8 Aug 2022 or the 2022 proxy. The diverse-director objective was phased in: one Diverse director by 2023, then two by 2025 (Global Select/Global Market) or 2026 (Capital Market). The deadlines were later moved to 31 December. Ended 4 Feb 2025.

measures.name: Board Diversity Matrix: gender identity counts
measures.definition: Annual standard table showing Total Number of Directors and the number who self-identify as Female, Male or Non-Binary, or did not disclose gender. Demographic background rows: African American or Black, Alaskan Native or Native American, Asian, Hispanic or Latinx, Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, White, Two or More Races or Ethnicities, LGBTQ+, did not disclose. 'Female' meant an individual who self-identifies her gender as a woman, without regard to designated sex at birth.

EU Directive 2022/2381 share of the underrepresented sex (by definition)

measures.name: Diverse director objective (comply or explain)
measures.definition: Have at least two Diverse directors, at least one self-identifying as Female and one as an Underrepresented Minority or LGBTQ+, or explain why not. Foreign issuers and smaller reporting companies could meet it with two Female directors, or one Female plus one other Diverse director.

EU Directive 2022/2381 40%/33% objectives (looks alike)
US-CA-SB826-AB979 quotas (looks alike: those were mandatory)

instruments.publicAccess: Public while in force: matrices in 2022-2024 proxy statements or on company websites. The historical matrices remain on EDGAR. Nothing new is required.
interop: Nasdaq aligned its race categories with the EEO-1 categories (by definition).
Foreign issuers had a separate matrix built on country-of-origin underrepresentation.

instruments.name: EEO-1 Component 1 (Employer Information Report, Standard Form 100)
instruments.jurisdiction: United States (federal; EEOC under Title VII section 709(c))
instruments.status: In force, but in limbo. The 2024 collection (Q4 2024 snapshot) ran 20 May to 24 Jun 2025 with sex reported as male or female only; the non-binary comment option was removed to comply with EO 14168. The 2025 collection (Q4 2025 snapshot) had not opened as of Oct 2026. The EEOC has proposed rescinding the report (see US-EEOC-NPRM-2026). The federal-contractor filing basis (EO 11246; 41 CFR 60-1.7) was revoked on 21 Jan 2025, yet the 2025 instructions still referred to contractors.
instruments.effective: Collected annually since 1966. Current rule: 29 CFR 1602.7, which states a 30 September deadline; the EEOC sets the actual window each year.
instruments.coverage: Private employers subject to Title VII with 100 or more employees, counted across affiliated companies of a single enterprise. Formerly also federal contractors with 50 or more employees and a contract of $50,000. Covers US establishments only.

measures.name: Employee counts by job category, sex and race/ethnicity
measures.definition: Number of employees in each of 10 EEO-1 job categories: Executive/Senior Level Officials and Managers; First/Mid-Level Officials and Managers; Professionals; Technicians; Sales Workers; Administrative Support Workers; Craft Workers; Operatives; Laborers and Helpers; Service Workers. Counted by sex (Male or Female; binary only from the 2024 report) and by race/ethnicity (Hispanic or Latino; White; Black or African American; Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander; Asian; American Indian or Alaska Native; Two or More Races).
measures.basis: Headcount. Full-time and part-time count equally; no FTE; no pay data.
measures.population: All employees on the US payroll in the snapshot pay period. Excludes non-US staff and workers not on the payroll. Multi-establishment employers file a consolidated (Type 2) report plus headquarters and establishment reports.
measures.period: One pay period of the employer's choice in Q4 (1 Oct to 31 Dec) of the reporting year. Filed 6 to 9 months later.
mapsTo: US-CA-GOV12999 headcounts (by definition: same 10 categories through RY2025; they diverge from RY2026 when California moves to 23 SOC-based categories)
US-MA-C149-105E (identical: the filed EEO-1 is submitted)
US-CO-HB26-1207 (identical by design: EEO-1 data in the form as it stood on 1 Mar 2026)
US-IL-EPA-S11 employee list (by definition: same gender and race categories, but individual records for the calendar year)
SASB '330a' workforce diversity metrics (official: the SASB technical protocols point US entities to the EEO-1 job categories)
% women in workforce or management under UK, EU, Japan, Australia WGEA and India BRSR (by definition only; populations, dates and management definitions differ)

measures.name: Women in management (derived by users, not an EEO-1 field)
measures.definition: Women's share of 'Executive/Senior Level Officials and Managers', or of that category plus 'First/Mid-Level Officials and Managers', calculated by data users from the counts.
measures.population: US payroll employees of the filer
mapsTo: Japan Act on Promotion of Women's Participation, ratio of women among managers (by definition; Japan's 'manager' is section chief and above)
Australia WGEA manager categories (by definition)
India BRSR KMP/board gender figures (looks alike only)

instruments.publicAccess: Not public. Title VII section 709(e) (42 USC 2000e-8(e)) makes it unlawful for EEOC staff to make the data public; the EEOC releases only aggregate tables. Two exceptions: (1) companies may publish their own reports (see US-EEO1-VOLUNTARY); (2) FOIA: the Ninth Circuit held on 30 Jul 2025 (CIR v. DOL; final 29 Dec 2025) that federal contractors' 2016-2020 Type 2 reports held by OFCCP are not 'commercial' information under FOIA Exemption 4. Release of withheld reports was scheduled from Feb 2026; completion was not confirmed.
interop: Through RY2025 California's pay data report uses the EEO-1 job categories and race/ethnicity/sex categories.
Massachusetts and Colorado take the EEO-1 itself as their state filing.

The earlier EEO-1 Component 2 (pay data for 2017 and 2018, collected 2019-20 under court order in NWLC v. OMB, then discontinued) used 12 BLS OES pay bands on W-2 Box 1 earnings plus hours worked. California's pay bands copy that design.
instruments.quote: and that has 100 or more employees shall file with the Commission

instruments.name: EEOC proposed rule to rescind EEO-1 to EEO-6 reporting and the related recordkeeping (29 CFR part 1602)
instruments.status: Proposed, not final (no final rule found in sources to about 22 Sep 2026). Commission vote 21 Jul 2026 (2-1: Chair Lucas and Commissioner Panuccio for, Commissioner Kotagal against). NPRM published 23 Jul 2026 at 91 FR 46332; public hearing 11 Aug 2026; comments closed 24 Aug 2026, with about 3,000 reported. It is unclear whether a final rule would cancel the 2025 cycle or take effect from the 2026 cycle. Legal challenge is likely; a 2017 attempt to stay EEO-1 Component 2 was vacated by a court in 2019.
instruments.effective: Not yet effective. Current obligations stay until a final rule takes effect.
instruments.coverage: Would remove EEO-1 (private employers with 100+ employees and certain federal contractors), EEO-3 (unions), EEO-4 (state and local governments), EEO-5 (school systems) and EEO-6 (higher education), plus the recordkeeping tied to them. Unaffected: UGESP demographic recordkeeping and OFCCP authority under Section 503 and VEVRAA.
instruments.publicAccess: The NPRM is public in the Federal Register. The underlying data are not public (see US-EEO1-C1).
interop: Massachusetts c.149 section 105E would likely lapse, because its coverage depends on being subject to the federal filing requirement (inference; no amendment found).
Colorado HB26-1207 is built to survive a federal repeal.
Illinois cut its EEO-1 dependency in 2025 (P.A. 104-0017).
California is independent of the EEO-1 and moves to its own categories from RY2026.

EEOC rationale as reported: collecting sex and race data 'may have the unintended consequence' of prompting discrimination, raises constitutional concerns, and imposes a burden the benefit does not justify.
instruments.source: https://www.littler.com/news-analysis/asap/eeoc-proposes-rescind-all-eeo-reporting-and-recordkeeping-requirements ; https://directemployers.org/2026/07/23/eeoc-eeo1-reporting-rescission-nprm-2026/ (secondary; the Federal Register text could not be fetched)

instruments.name: Voluntary publication of the consolidated EEO-1 report by listed companies
instruments.status: Voluntary practice. It peaked in 2023-24 after shareholder proposals, the NYC Comptroller's agreements with companies and investor campaigns: HR Policy Association counted 386 S&P 500 companies publishing or committed to publish by early 2024, up from 52 at end-2020. It fell back in 2025-26; a vendor estimate (unverified) puts it at just under 60% of the S&P 500 and 37% of the Russell 1000. Because the 2025 collection never opened, the latest EEO-1 most companies can publish is the Q4 2024 snapshot. SLB 14M (Feb 2025) made shareholder proposals asking for EEO-1 publication easier to exclude.
instruments.effective: n/a (voluntary; tracked since about 2019)
instruments.coverage: Mainly large US-listed companies. They publish the consolidated (Type 2) report of the US filer.

measures.name: Published consolidated EEO-1 table
measures.definition: A copy or reproduction of the company's filed EEO-1 Component 1 consolidated report: counts by job category, sex and race/ethnicity.
measures.basis: Headcount; full-time and part-time count equally
measures.population: US payroll employees of the EEO-1 filing enterprise, not the global listed group
measures.period: Q4 pay-period snapshot of the report year, usually published 6 to 18 months later
mapsTo: US-EEO1-C1 (identical when the filed form is published unaltered)
SASB '330a' diversity metrics (official reference to EEO-1 categories)
Non-US % women metrics (by definition only)

instruments.quote: publicly disclosing an EEO-1 Survey is the gold standard (JUST Capital, Dec 2019)

instruments.name: California pay data reporting: Government Code section 12999 (SB 973 of 2020, SB 1162 of 2022, SB 464 of 2025)
instruments.status: In force. Reports for Reporting Year 2025 were due 13 May 2026; RY2025 added fields for exemption status (exempt or non-exempt), employment type (full-time, part-time or intermittent) and weeks worked. SB 464 was signed 13 Oct 2025. From 1 Jan 2026: demographic data must be stored apart from personnel records, and penalties become mandatory when CRD asks a court for them ($100 per employee, $200 for repeat violations). On 1 Jan 2027 the current version sunsets and a new version requires 23 job categories aligned with the Standard Occupational Classification (SOC), first used for RY2026 reports due 12 May 2027.
instruments.effective: SB 973: first reports 31 Mar 2021 (RY2020). SB 1162: from 1 Jan 2023 (deadline the second Wednesday of May; labor contractor reports; mean and median hourly rates; the option to file the federal EEO-1 instead was removed). SB 464: 1 Jan 2026 and 1 Jan 2027.
instruments.coverage: Private employers with 100+ payroll employees, counting California and non-California staff. areas.notes:
US scope, state as of 12 Oct 2026.

WHAT IS PUBLIC AND WHAT IS NOT
- Public: SEC Item 101(c) human capital text and Item 407 nominee-diversity narrative (both on EDGAR, both in the issuer's own terms); Nasdaq Board Diversity Matrices for 2022-2024 (historical only); Washington board diversity discussions (in proxies); Illinois section 8.12 board and officer demographics (Secretary of State filings and the IGPA report); New York section 408 women-director counts (biennial statements); California SB 826 compliance reports 2019-21 (historical); EEO-1 tables that companies publish voluntarily; federal contractors' 2016-2020 EEO-1 Type 2 reports, which became releasable under FOIA after CIR v. DOL (9th Cir. 2025).
- Aggregates only: EEOC national EEO-1 tables; Massachusetts EOLWD sector reports; California CRD (may publish aggregates).
- Not public: EEO-1 Component 1 filings (Title VII section 709(e)); the discontinued Component 2 pay data; California pay data reports (exempt from the Public Records Act); Illinois EPRC data (confidential); individual Massachusetts reports; Colorado HB26-1207 filings (confidentiality not confirmed); contractor affirmative action plans.
- No US instrument publishes a company-level gender pay gap. Where one exists, it is voluntary and usually an 'adjusted' pay-equity figure.

WHAT IS GENUINELY INTEROPERABLE
1. EEO-1 Component 1 is the common spine of the US regimes. Massachusetts files the EEO-1 itself. Colorado HB26-1207 freezes the 1 Mar 2026 EEO-1 form and survives a federal repeal. California uses the EEO-1 job and demographic categories through RY2025. Illinois used them until P.A. 104-0017 (2025). SASB '330a' protocols point US entities to the EEO-1 job categories. Within the US, headcount by sex x job category maps one to one across these regimes up to the RY2025 data.
2. California's pay bands copy the discontinued EEO-1 Component 2 (BLS OES bands plus hours). The definitions match, but Component 2 used W-2 Box 1 while California uses total W-2 earnings (Box 5 per CRD).
3. Board 'Female' counts: Nasdaq and California SB 826 used the same self-identification definition. Washington ('self-identify as women'), New York section 408 and Illinois section 8.12 match by definition.
4. Pay-range-in-posting laws (CA, CO, NY/NYC, WA, IL, MA and others) map by definition to EU Directive 2023/970 Art. 5. They produce no gender data.
- No official document ties any US gender measure to UK, EU, Japanese, Australian or Indian measures. Every cross-border mapping is 'by definition' or 'looks alike'.

WHAT ONLY LOOKS ALIKE
- California's 'mean and median hourly rate' is not a gender pay gap. It is one rate per job category x race x sex cell, derived from annual W-2 total earnings divided by annual hours, for California staff only. No gap is computed. The UK figure uses ordinary hourly pay in one April pay period across the whole employer, with bonus separate. The EU Directive uses gross annual and hourly pay including complementary components. Japan uses a ratio of annual average wages. Australia's WGEA uses annualised FTE total remuneration.
- Illinois 'average compensation not consistently below' is a self-certification, not a published gap. It resembles the EU Art. 10 joint-assessment trigger but has no 5% threshold.
- EEO-1 'Executive/Senior Level Officials and Managers' is not UK 'senior management', Japan's managers (section chief and above) or India BRSR KMP.
- Item 101(c) headcount is not the EEO-1 total.
- Voluntary US 'pay equity' (adjusted, same role) figures are not unadjusted gaps.

TRAPS
- Hourly versus annual: EEO-1 has no pay at all. California hourly rates come from calendar-year totals. Illinois collects annual total wages (or mean hourly for hourly staff). Pay transparency ranges are base pay only.
- Mean versus median: California reports both per cell. Illinois uses averages. US voluntary disclosures mix them.
- Base versus total: California and Illinois use total taxable earnings, including bonus, overtime and RSU income. Pay transparency laws use base pay.
- Permanent versus all staff: EEO-1 and California count everyone on payroll, including part-time and temporary staff, with no FTE weighting. California reports labor-contractor workers separately. Illinois includes leavers during the year. Item 101(c) is whatever the registrant says.
- Snapshot dates: EEO-1 and California use one Q4 pay period of the employer's choice (Oct to Dec); California and Illinois pay data cover the calendar year; Item 101(c) usually fiscal year-end. Massachusetts files the 'most recent' EEO-1, so the Feb 2026 filing held the Q4 2024 snapshot. No Q4 2025 EEO-1 exists, because the 2025 collection never opened.
- Reporting entity versus listed group: the EEO-1 covers the US enterprise only (Type 2 consolidated), never the global group. California covers California employees of the filer or its integrated enterprise; Illinois covers Illinois employees; Massachusetts may be state-only. A foreign-listed group's US subsidiaries file separately. SEC items cover the consolidated registrant worldwide.
- Sex basis: EEO-1 is binary-only from the 2024 report (EO 14168), and Colorado freezes that form. Nasdaq, California SB 826 and Washington used self-identified gender, and Nasdaq had a Non-Binary category.
- Pending changes: the EEOC rescission NPRM (91 FR 46332) would end the federal series, and Massachusetts coverage falls with it. California switches to 23 SOC-based categories for RY2026 (due May 2027), which breaks comparability with earlier years and with the EEO-1.

CAVEATS
- The shared web-search budget ran out partway through. These were not checked after the dates of the latest sources: a final EEOC rule (sources to about 22 Sep 2026); SEC action after mid-2026 on Regulation S-K or the AFL petition; the status of the California SB 826/AB 979 appeals (latest source Jan 2025); the Nasdaq rulebook text; the text of Illinois section 8.12; Colorado HB26-1207's confidentiality and publication rules; the exact effective dates of the state pay transparency laws.
